board_events.text: PRONG 1 — REDUCE BIRTHS: motivate smaller families using contraceptive methods. This is the menu from subtopic 01.
PRONG 2 — DELAY REPRODUCTION: statutory raising of the marriageable age. 18 YEARS FOR FEMALES, 21 YEARS FOR MALES.
Raising the marriageable age shortens each woman's reproductive window and spaces generations. Cue: 'ladies first, and the smaller number' — female 18.
REINFORCEMENT: incentives to couples with small families. Reward, not compulsion.
Contraceptives are PROMOTED, never banned. An option offering 'banning all contraceptives' inverts the logic — banning them would RAISE births.
SCALE (NCERT-illustrative): world population was around 2 billion in 1900 and rose to about 6 billion by 2000. India's grew from roughly 350 million at independence to over 1 billion by 2000.
LIMITING CONDITION: 'small family' incentives assume couples have real, accessible choices — which is the contraceptive menu of subtopic 01. Without access, motivation is empty.

segments.text: Before the strategies, the problem list. And there is a reason to take this list seriously rather than skim it — a five-mark question that asks you to suggest steps to improve reproductive health is really asking which of these fronts you can name.
Look at the board. Seven items, and notice the colour coding — some of them you have already studied under different headings.

Here is how N C E R T groups them. Population explosion. Infertility. Sexually transmitted diseases. Complications of abortion. Menstrual problems. Pregnancy and delivery related problems. And the broader health of mothers. Seven fronts, all live at once.

Now notice how much of that map you already hold. Infertility and sexually transmitted diseases were the whole of the previous subtopic. Complications of abortion belong with medical termination of pregnancy, which is coming next. Population explosion is this subtopic. The chapter is not a set of unrelated topics — it is this list, unpacked one item at a time.

And that gives you the sentence to write in a long answer. Every strategy targets one or more of these problems. Which is exactly why improving reproductive health is never a single fix. It is a coordinated package — you cannot solve seven fronts with one tool.

It also explains something we said two sections ago. This is why the World Health Organisation definition needed four aspects. Look at that list — menstrual problems are physical, attitudes to sex are emotional and behavioural, and a skewed sex ratio is social. A list this wide simply cannot be covered by absence of disease alone.

Now the limiting condition, and it is the honest part of this subtopic. Awareness and statutory measures only work when they are implemented and when they are accepted. Both. A programme that exists on paper, that nobody delivers or nobody trusts, changes nothing.

<whisper>Hold that thought, because it returns with force later in this subtopic. A law on paper — like the ban on sex-determination — does not by itself end a social evil if attitudes do not change. That is why sex education keeps appearing on the strategy list alongside the statutes. The statute is necessary. It has never been sufficient.

We have the problem list. Now the strategy list. But do not learn it as six bullet points to recite — learn what each pillar actually changes, and where in the system it acts. That is what turns a three-mark answer into a five-mark one.

Look at the three main pillars across the board. Education, awareness, medical facilities. And notice the small print under each — foundation, extends it to the public, acts downstream. Three different points of intervention.

Pillar one, sex education in schools, and it is called the foundation for a reason. It gives adolescents correct information about reproductive organs, about the changes of adolescence, about safe and hygienic sexual practices, and about sexually transmitted diseases.

And here is its mechanism, which is the bit worth writing. It replaces myth and misconception with fact, so that young people make safer choices. Note the causal chain — information, then better choices, then better outcomes. Counselling at school level supports adolescents through these changes. This pillar does not treat anybody. It prevents.

Pillar two, awareness-building. This is the same idea extended from the classroom to the wider public. It covers the dangers of uncontrolled population growth, and the need to prevent social evils such as sex-abuse and sex-related crime. Notice that last one — reproductive health strategy explicitly includes preventing sexual crime. That is on the N C E R T list, and students routinely forget it.

Pillar three, better medical facilities, and this one acts downstream — after the problem exists rather than before. Prenatal screening. Hygienic and medically-assisted deliveries. Postnatal care of mother and infant. And the effect is direct and measurable — these reduce maternal mortality rate and infant mortality rate. Improved detection and cure of sexually transmitted diseases raises the population's reproductive health the same way.

And the last pillar, easy to skip and easy to ask about. Research is encouraged, to develop safer methods. N C E R T's own example is Saheli, developed at the Central Drug Research Institute, C D R I, Lucknow. You met Saheli as a contraceptive in subtopic one. Here it reappears as evidence that the research pillar works.

<whisper>So when a question hands you a strategy and asks what it achieves, do not answer improves reproductive health. Answer with the mechanism. Education replaces myth with fact and produces safer choices. Medical facilities cut M M R and I M R. Research produces safer methods. Each pillar has its own verb.
This section is short, it is guaranteed marks, and it is the one students most often treat as filler. It is not filler. It is the logical closing of everything the last two sections set up.
Look at the board. Five green boxes, and then two verdict boxes underneath — one for trends moving this way, one for trends moving the other way.

Start from the frame. Reproductive health is treated not as a private medical matter but as a social goal that a country plans for. That is exactly why India built national programmes around it rather than leaving it to individual doctors and individual families.

And here is the consequence that most students never draw. A goal you plan for is a goal you must measure. You cannot budget for something and then have no way of knowing whether it worked. That is the entire role of the indicators — they are not a list, they are the measuring instrument.

So here they are, five of them. Better awareness about sex-related matters. Decreased maternal mortality rate and infant mortality rate. An increased number of medically-assisted deliveries. Smaller families. And better detection and cure of sexually transmitted diseases.

Notice what those five have in common. Every one of them is countable. Improvement is measured not by slogans but by indicators. Nobody claims success because a campaign felt persuasive — they claim it because the infant mortality rate fell.

<whisper>Now the exam pattern, and it is remarkably consistent. The question hands you a cluster of these trends — falling M M R, more assisted deliveries, smaller families — and asks what they signify. The intended answer is one line. A reproductively healthier society, or a successful R C H strategy. Read indicators, conclude, in one step. Do not narrate each trend.

And run it in reverse too, because that version is asked as well. A rising sex-ratio imbalance, or a rising incidence of sexually transmitted diseases, signals that the strategies are failing and need reinforcement — through stronger awareness, sex education, and enforcement of the sex-determination ban. Same instrument, opposite reading.

Picture a bucket filling with water while the drain at the bottom is slowly being plugged. If water pours in faster than it drains, the bucket overflows. That overflow is exactly what happened to the human population, and this section is the biology of the drain.

Look at the two panels. On the left, the historic picture — two lines tracking each other. On the right, the twentieth century, where one line falls and the other does not. The orange band between them is the whole topic.

Start with the one line everything reduces to. A population grows when the birth rate exceeds the death rate. That is not a fact to memorise, it is the tool you test every option against. Any option that has deaths outpacing births describes a shrinking population, and you can reject it without further thought.

Now the historic picture. A population stays roughly in balance when a high birth rate is matched by a high death rate. Many children born, many children lost. Grim, but stable. Growth is slow because the two lines track each other.

Then the twentieth century breaks the symmetry. Better health facilities caused a rapid decline in the death rate, and with it the maternal mortality rate and the infant mortality rate. But the birth rate stayed high. One line fell. The other did not follow.

<curious>Why did they not fall together? Because they respond to different things. Advances in medicine, vaccination, sanitation, and food security cut the death rate first and fastest — a vaccine works the year it arrives. But birth rates are cultural. They fall slowly, over generations, as expectations change. That mismatch in speed opened a wide gap, and during that gap the population surged.

Two more contributors finish the picture. A larger number of people reaching reproducible age — more survivors from the previous cohort means more potential parents in this one. And better living conditions generally. Put it all together and the net addition each year became explosive.

And the consequence is the part the board question wants. Pressure on the most basic requirements — food, shelter, clothing, water. Left unchecked, that pressure deepens poverty, unemployment, and resource scarcity. Which is exactly why population stabilisation is treated as a precondition for reproductive health rather than as a separate goal sitting beside it.

<whisper>And now the sentence that shows you have actually understood this. Policy can only close the gap from the births side. Why? Because the deaths side — longer lives, fewer mothers dying, fewer infants dying — is precisely the outcome we were trying to achieve. Nobody wants to fix population by raising the death rate. The falling death rate is not the problem. It is the success.

The mechanism said policy can only work from the births side. So what does working from the births side actually look like? Three measures, and N C E R T asks for them as a list often enough that you should be able to write them without thinking.
Look at the board. Three boxes, but notice they are not three parallel things. Read the strip underneath — the response is two-pronged, and the third measure reinforces the other two.

Prong one, reduce births. Motivate smaller families using contraceptive methods. And notice the word — motivate. Not compel. This is the entire menu from subtopic one, deployed as public policy rather than personal choice. All that work on the five families pays off right here.

Prong two, delay reproduction. Statutory raising of the marriageable age. Eighteen years for females. Twenty one years for males. Learn those two numbers as a pair, in that order, because the trap option simply reverses them.

<curious>But why does raising the marriageable age reduce population at all? It does not stop anyone having children. Here is the logic. It shortens each woman's reproductive window — fewer fertile years available means fewer children possible. And it spaces generations — if each generation starts later, generations pile up more slowly. Two effects, one law. And the memory cue if the numbers slip: ladies first, and the smaller number. Female eighteen.

Third, reinforcement. Incentives to couples with small families. This is reward rather than compulsion, and it works alongside the other two rather than replacing them. Motivation, plus a statutory floor, plus a reason to act.

<whisper>Now the option that appears every year and catches the careless. Banning all contraceptives is not a population control measure. Contraceptives are promoted, never banned. Read that option slowly and you see it inverts the logic — banning contraceptives would raise births, not lower them. A student rushing the word control can misread it as any restriction. It is not.

Finally, the scale, because N C E R T gives illustrative figures and C U E T likes them. The world population was around two billion in nineteen hundred, and rose to about six billion by the year two thousand. Tripled in a century. And India's grew from roughly three hundred and fifty million at independence to over one billion by two thousand.

One limiting condition to close on, and it is an honest one. Small family incentives assume that couples have real, accessible choices — which means the contraceptive menu of subtopic one has to actually reach them. Without access, motivation is empty. You cannot incentivise a decision somebody has no means to act on.

Strategies से पहले problem list. और इसे skim करने की जगह गंभीरता से लेने की एक वजह है — जो पाँच-mark question reproductive health सुधारने के steps पूछता है, वो असल में पूछ रहा है कि इन fronts में से आप कितने नाम ले सकते हैं।
Board देखिए। सात items, और colour coding notice कीजिए — इनमें से कुछ आप दूसरे headings के नीचे पढ़ चुके हैं।

N C E R T इन्हें ऐसे group करता है। Population explosion. Infertility. Sexually transmitted diseases. Complications of abortion. Menstrual problems. Pregnancy और delivery से जुड़ी problems. और mothers की व्यापक health. सात fronts, सब एक साथ ज़िंदा।

अब notice कीजिए यह map आपके पास कितना पहले से है। Infertility और sexually transmitted diseases तो पूरा पिछला subtopic थे। Complications of abortion medical termination of pregnancy के साथ आते हैं, जो अगला है। Population explosion यही subtopic है। Chapter अलग-अलग topics का ढेर नहीं है — यह वही list है, एक-एक item खोलकर।

और इसी से आपको वो sentence मिलती है जो long answer में लिखनी है। हर strategy इनमें से एक या ज़्यादा problems को target करती है। इसीलिए reproductive health सुधारना कभी single fix नहीं होता। यह एक coordinated package है — सात fronts एक tool से हल नहीं होते।

और इससे वो बात भी समझ आती है जो हमने दो sections पहले कही थी। इसीलिए World Health Organisation की definition को चार aspects चाहिए थे। उस list को देखिए — menstrual problems physical हैं, sex को लेकर attitudes emotional और behavioural हैं, और skewed sex ratio social है। इतनी चौड़ी list को सिर्फ़ बीमारी का न होना cover कर ही नहीं सकता।

अब limiting condition, और यही इस subtopic का ईमानदार हिस्सा है। Awareness और statutory measures तभी काम करते हैं जब वो implement हों और accept भी हों। दोनों। जो programme काग़ज़ पर है, जिसे कोई पहुँचाता नहीं या कोई भरोसा नहीं करता, वो कुछ नहीं बदलता।

<whisper>इस बात को पकड़े रखिए, क्योंकि यह इसी subtopic में आगे पूरी ताक़त से लौटती है। काग़ज़ पर लिखा क़ानून — जैसे sex-determination पर ban — अपने आप किसी social evil को ख़त्म नहीं करता, अगर attitudes न बदलें। इसीलिए strategy list में statutes के साथ-साथ sex education बार-बार आता है। Statute ज़रूरी है। काफ़ी कभी नहीं रहा।

Problem list मिल गई। अब strategy list. लेकिन इसे छह bullet points की तरह रटिए मत — यह सीखिए कि हर pillar असल में क्या बदलता है, और system में कहाँ act करता है। यही तीन-mark answer को पाँच-mark answer बनाता है।

Board पर तीनों main pillars देखिए। Education, awareness, medical facilities. और हर एक के नीचे छोटा text notice कीजिए — foundation, public तक फैलाता है, downstream act करता है। तीन अलग जगहों पर intervention.

Pillar एक, schools में sex education, और इसे foundation कहने की वजह है। यह adolescents को reproductive organs के बारे में, adolescence के बदलावों के बारे में, safe और hygienic sexual practices के बारे में, और sexually transmitted diseases के बारे में सही जानकारी देता है।

और अब इसका mechanism, जो लिखने लायक़ हिस्सा है। यह myth और misconception की जगह fact रखता है, ताकि young people safer choices करें। Causal chain notice कीजिए — जानकारी, फिर बेहतर choices, फिर बेहतर outcomes. School level पर counselling adolescents को इन बदलावों में सहारा देती है। यह pillar किसी का इलाज नहीं करता। यह रोकता है।

Pillar दो, awareness-building. यही idea classroom से निकलकर आम जनता तक। इसमें uncontrolled population growth के ख़तरे आते हैं, और sex-abuse तथा sex-related crime जैसी social evils को रोकने की ज़रूरत। आख़िरी वाला notice कीजिए — reproductive health strategy में sexual crime रोकना साफ़-साफ़ शामिल है। यह N C E R T की list पर है, और students इसे अक्सर भूल जाते हैं।

Pillar तीन, better medical facilities, और यह downstream act करता है — problem होने के बाद, पहले नहीं। Prenatal screening. Hygienic और medically-assisted deliveries. Mother और infant की postnatal care. और असर सीधा और measurable है — ये maternal mortality rate और infant mortality rate को कम करते हैं। Sexually transmitted diseases की बेहतर detection और cure उसी तरह आबादी की reproductive health बढ़ाती है।

और आख़िरी pillar, जिसे छोड़ना आसान है और जिस पर पूछना भी आसान। Research को encourage किया जाता है, safer methods बनाने के लिए। N C E R T का अपना example है Saheli, जो Central Drug Research Institute, यानी C D R I, Lucknow में बना। Saheli से आप subtopic एक में contraceptive की तरह मिल चुके हैं। यहाँ वो इस बात के सबूत की तरह लौटता है कि research pillar काम करता है।

<whisper>तो जब कोई question आपको strategy देकर पूछे कि यह क्या हासिल करती है, तो जवाब मत दीजिए reproductive health सुधरती है। जवाब mechanism से दीजिए। Education myth की जगह fact रखता है और safer choices लाता है। Medical facilities M M R और I M R घटाती हैं। Research safer methods देता है। हर pillar का अपना verb है।
यह section छोटा है, यहाँ marks पक्के हैं, और यही वो है जिसे students अक्सर filler समझ लेते हैं। यह filler नहीं है। यह पिछले दो sections ने जो खड़ा किया, उसका logical समापन है।
Board देखिए। पाँच green boxes, और नीचे दो verdict boxes — एक इस तरफ़ जाते trends के लिए, एक उलटी तरफ़ जाते trends के लिए।

Frame से शुरू कीजिए। Reproductive health को private medical मामला नहीं, बल्कि एक social goal माना जाता है जिसकी country planning करती है। इसीलिए India ने इसके इर्द-गिर्द national programmes बनाए, इसे individual doctors और individual families पर नहीं छोड़ा।

और अब वो नतीजा जो ज़्यादातर students कभी नहीं निकालते। जिस goal की planning करते हैं, उसे measure भी करना पड़ता है। आप किसी चीज़ का budget बनाकर यह नहीं कह सकते कि पता ही नहीं चला काम हुआ या नहीं। यही indicators का पूरा role है — ये कोई list नहीं, ये measuring instrument हैं।

तो ये रहे, पाँच। Sex-related मामलों में बेहतर awareness. घटी हुई maternal mortality rate और infant mortality rate. Medically-assisted deliveries की बढ़ी हुई संख्या। छोटे families. और sexually transmitted diseases की बेहतर detection और cure.

Notice कीजिए इन पाँचों में common क्या है। हर एक गिना जा सकता है। सुधार slogans से नहीं, indicators से मापा जाता है। कोई इसलिए success का दावा नहीं करता कि campaign असरदार लगा — दावा इसलिए करता है कि infant mortality rate गिरी।

<whisper>अब exam pattern, और यह हैरान करने वाली हद तक consistent है। Question आपको इन trends का एक cluster देता है — गिरती M M R, ज़्यादा assisted deliveries, छोटे families — और पूछता है कि ये क्या दिखाते हैं। मनचाहा answer एक line है। एक reproductively healthier society, या एक successful R C H strategy. Indicators पढ़िए, conclusion दीजिए, एक ही step में। हर trend का बयान मत कीजिए।

और इसे उलटा भी चलाइए, क्योंकि वो version भी पूछा जाता है। बढ़ता sex-ratio imbalance, या sexually transmitted diseases की बढ़ती incidence, यह signal है कि strategies fail हो रही हैं और उन्हें मज़बूती चाहिए — ज़्यादा awareness से, sex education से, और sex-determination ban के enforcement से। वही instrument, उलटी reading.

एक bucket सोचिए जिसमें पानी भर रहा है और नीचे की drain धीरे-धीरे बंद की जा रही है। अगर पानी drain होने से तेज़ आए, तो bucket छलक जाएगा। इंसानी आबादी के साथ ठीक यही हुआ, और यह section उस drain की biology है।
दोनों panels देखिए। बाईं तरफ़ ऐतिहासिक तस्वीर — दो lines एक-दूसरे के साथ चलती हुईं। दाईं तरफ़ बीसवीं सदी, जहाँ एक line गिरती है और दूसरी नहीं। उनके बीच का orange band ही पूरा topic है।

उस एक line से शुरू कीजिए जिस पर सब कुछ सिमटता है। आबादी तब बढ़ती है जब birth rate, death rate से ज़्यादा हो। यह रटने का fact नहीं, वो tool है जिससे आप हर option test करते हैं। जो option deaths को births से आगे दिखाए, वो सिकुड़ती आबादी बता रहा है, और उसे बिना सोचे reject कर सकते हैं।

अब ऐतिहासिक तस्वीर। आबादी लगभग balance में रहती है जब high birth rate के सामने high death rate हो। बहुत बच्चे पैदा, बहुत बच्चे खोए। कड़वा, लेकिन stable. Growth धीमी है क्योंकि दोनों lines साथ चलती हैं।

फिर बीसवीं सदी यह symmetry तोड़ती है। बेहतर health facilities ने death rate में तेज़ गिरावट लाई, और उसके साथ maternal mortality rate और infant mortality rate में भी। लेकिन birth rate high ही रहा। एक line गिरी। दूसरी साथ नहीं आई।

<curious>दोनों साथ क्यों नहीं गिरीं? क्योंकि दोनों अलग चीज़ों पर react करती हैं। Medicine, vaccination, sanitation, और food security में तरक़्क़ी ने death rate को पहले और सबसे तेज़ काटा — vaccine जिस साल आता है, उसी साल काम करता है। लेकिन birth rates cultural हैं। वो धीरे गिरते हैं, पीढ़ियों में, जैसे-जैसे उम्मीदें बदलती हैं। रफ़्तार का यही फ़र्क़ एक चौड़ा gap खोल गया, और उसी gap में आबादी उछल पड़ी।

दो और contributors तस्वीर पूरी करते हैं। Reproducible age तक पहुँचने वाले लोगों की बढ़ी संख्या — पिछली cohort से ज़्यादा बचे लोग यानी इस cohort में ज़्यादा संभावित माता-पिता। और आम तौर पर बेहतर living conditions. सब जोड़िए और हर साल का net addition explosive हो गया।

और consequence वो हिस्सा है जो board question चाहता है। सबसे बुनियादी ज़रूरतों पर दबाव — food, shelter, clothing, पानी। बिना रोके यह दबाव poverty, unemployment, और resource scarcity को गहरा करता है। इसीलिए population stabilisation को reproductive health की precondition माना जाता है, न कि उसके बगल में रखा कोई अलग goal.

<whisper>और अब वो sentence जो दिखाती है कि आपने यह सच में समझा है। Policy सिर्फ़ births वाली तरफ़ से gap बंद कर सकती है। क्यों? क्योंकि deaths वाली तरफ़ — लंबी ज़िंदगी, कम mothers की मौत, कम infants की मौत — वही तो हासिल करना था। कोई भी death rate बढ़ाकर population ठीक नहीं करना चाहता। गिरती death rate problem नहीं है। वो success है।

Mechanism ने कहा कि policy सिर्फ़ births वाली तरफ़ से काम कर सकती है। तो births वाली तरफ़ से काम करना दिखता कैसा है? तीन measures, और N C E R T इन्हें list की तरह इतनी बार पूछता है कि आपको ये बिना सोचे लिखने आने चाहिए।
Board देखिए। तीन boxes, लेकिन notice कीजिए ये तीन समानांतर चीज़ें नहीं हैं। नीचे की strip पढ़िए — response two-pronged है, और तीसरा measure बाक़ी दोनों को मज़बूत करता है।

Prong एक, births कम कीजिए। Contraceptive methods से छोटे families के लिए motivate कीजिए। और शब्द notice कीजिए — motivate. मजबूर नहीं। यह subtopic एक का पूरा menu है, जो personal choice की जगह public policy बनकर उतरता है। पाँच families पर की गई सारी मेहनत यहीं काम आती है।

Prong दो, reproduction को delay कीजिए। Statutory तौर पर marriageable age बढ़ाना। Females के लिए eighteen years. Males के लिए twenty one years. इन दोनों numbers को जोड़ी की तरह, इसी order में सीखिए, क्योंकि trap option बस इन्हें उलट देता है।

<curious>लेकिन marriageable age बढ़ाने से आबादी कम क्यों होती है? यह तो किसी को बच्चे होने से नहीं रोकता। Logic यह है। यह हर woman की reproductive window छोटी कर देता है — कम fertile साल यानी कम बच्चे मुमकिन। और यह generations को space करता है — हर पीढ़ी देर से शुरू हो तो पीढ़ियाँ धीरे जमा होती हैं। दो असर, एक क़ानून। और numbers फिसलें तो memory cue: ladies first, and the smaller number. Female eighteen.

तीसरा, reinforcement. छोटे families वाले couples को incentives. यह मजबूरी नहीं, इनाम है, और यह बाक़ी दोनों की जगह लेने के बजाय उनके साथ चलता है। Motivation, plus एक statutory floor, plus act करने की वजह।

<whisper>अब वो option जो हर साल आता है और लापरवाह को पकड़ लेता है। सारे contraceptives पर ban लगाना population control measure नहीं है। Contraceptives promote किए जाते हैं, ban कभी नहीं। उस option को धीरे पढ़िए तो दिखेगा कि यह logic ही उलट देता है — contraceptives ban करने से births बढ़ेंगे, घटेंगे नहीं। जल्दबाज़ी में control शब्द पढ़ने वाला student इसे कोई भी पाबंदी समझ सकता है। यह वो नहीं है।

आख़िर में scale, क्योंकि N C E R T illustrative figures देता है और C U E T को वो पसंद हैं। दुनिया की आबादी nineteen hundred में लगभग two billion थी, और साल two thousand तक लगभग six billion हो गई। एक सदी में तिगुनी। और India की आबादी independence के वक़्त लगभग three hundred fifty million से बढ़कर two thousand तक one billion से ऊपर पहुँच गई।

एक limiting condition पर ख़त्म कीजिए, और यह ईमानदार है। Small family incentives यह मानकर चलते हैं कि couples के पास असली, पहुँच में आने वाले choices हैं — यानी subtopic एक का contraceptive menu उन तक सच में पहुँचे। Access के बिना motivation खोखला है। जिस फ़ैसले पर अमल का ज़रिया ही न हो, उस पर incentive नहीं दिया जा सकता।

board_events.text: AMNIOCENTESIS: a prenatal test that withdraws a sample of the AMNIOTIC FLUID surrounding the foetus. The foetal cells in it reveal the chromosomal pattern and genetic disorders.
LEGITIMATE USE: detecting conditions such as Down syndrome or haemophilia. This is a valuable diagnostic tool.
THE MISUSE: because the chromosomal pattern also reveals FOETAL SEX, the test has been abused for prenatal sex-determination — leading to FEMALE FOETICIDE and a dangerously skewed sex ratio.
WHY IT MATTERS: a society that systematically aborts female foetuses develops a skewed, male-biased sex ratio — fewer women, disrupted marriage patterns, and entrenched gender injustice.

THE RESPONSE: a statutory ban on using such techniques for sex-determination. In India, the Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act, 1994 — making prenatal sex-determination a punishable offence.

Only the MISUSE is banned. The diagnostic use is legal and valuable. And because attitudes, not just statutes, drive the practice, sex education and awareness are treated as equally essential to enforcement.
CROSS-LINK: female foeticide is carried out through MTP misuse — the subject of subtopic 04.

A: A statutory ban has been placed on the use of amniocentesis for sex-determination. R: Amniocentesis cannot detect any genetic disorder of the foetus. [NEET, high difficulty]

board_events.text: TEST A: yes — prenatal sex-determination is banned, by the PCPNDT Act of 1994, to curb female foeticide. A is TRUE.
TEST R: amniocentesis is PRIMARILY a tool to detect genetic and chromosomal disorders. Saying it cannot is FALSE.
A true, R false. ANSWER: (c). Once R is false, the question of whether R explains A does not arise.
TRAP: the ban is on the MISUSE (sex-determination), NOT on the legitimate diagnostic use. Students who conflate the two may wrongly accept R.
Notice the shape of the trap: R is not a random false statement. It is precisely the false statement a student would produce if they believed amniocentesis ITSELF had been outlawed.
Follow that reasoning: something got banned; bans are for bad things; so amniocentesis must be bad; so it must not detect disorders. R now sounds plausible — and they mark (a).

segments.text: <curious>Here is a genuinely uncomfortable question. Can a piece of medical technology be good and evil at the same time? Amniocentesis is the chapter's answer, and the way the law handles it is what the exam actually tests.
Look at the board. A green strip at the top, a red chain across the middle, and a legal cross struck through it. The green and the red are the same technique.

The technique first. Amniocentesis withdraws a sample of the amniotic fluid surrounding the foetus. That fluid contains foetal cells, and those cells reveal the chromosomal pattern and any genetic disorders. Note the sample precisely — amniotic fluid. Not maternal blood, not placental tissue, not cervical mucus. Options offer all three.

And the legitimate purpose is genuinely valuable. It detects conditions such as Down syndrome or haemophilia, before birth, when a family can prepare or a clinician can plan. This is a good tool. Hold on to that, because we are about to describe something terrible.

Now the misuse. The chromosomal pattern does not only reveal disorders. It also reveals foetal sex. And so the test has been abused for prenatal sex-determination, and that leads to female foeticide — the selective abortion of female foetuses — and to a dangerously skewed sex ratio. The technique did not change. The purpose did.

Why does this matter so much? Because a society that systematically aborts female foetuses develops a skewed, male-biased sex ratio, and the consequences run for generations. Fewer women in the population. Disrupted marriage patterns. Entrenched gender injustice. The ban therefore protects not just individual foetuses but the demographic and social balance of society itself.

So the strategy in response is statutory. A ban on using such techniques for sex-determination. In India that is the Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques Act, of nineteen ninety four, the P C P N D T Act. It makes prenatal sex-determination a punishable offence.

<whisper>And now the precision the exam is actually testing. Only the misuse is banned. The diagnostic use is legal and valuable and continues. Amniocentesis is not outlawed — sex-determination is. Students conflate the two constantly, and an entire assertion reason question is built on that confusion. And remember the limiting condition — because attitudes, not just statutes, drive the practice, sex education and awareness are treated as equally essential to enforcement.

One cross-link before we leave. How is female foeticide actually carried out? Through the misuse of medical termination of pregnancy. Sex-determination identifies the foetus; M T P ends the pregnancy. That is the next subtopic, and this is where the two connect.
Five marks, and it is the most predictable question in the subtopic. Which cuts both ways — it is free marks if you have the structure, and it is a rambling half-answer if you do not.

Read the command words. Define, and suggest three. That is two separate tasks with two separate mark allocations. So your answer has two visible parts, and the examiner should be able to see both at a glance.

And note what suggest three actually demands. Three distinct strategies. Not three rewordings of one strategy dressed up differently. A script that says educate people, then teach students, then spread information has written one strategy three times and will be paid for one.
Look at the board. One definition strip on top, three separate boxes underneath, and one reserve box. That is the shape of a full-mark answer.

The definition, in one line, all four aspects. Reproductive health is total well-being in the physical, emotional, behavioural, and social aspects of reproduction. Do not write a paragraph. Do not drop social. One line, four words.
Strategy one. Introduce sex education in schools, to dispel myths. And add the purpose clause — to dispel myths — because it shows you know the mechanism rather than just the label.

Strategy two, and notice it is a completely different kind of intervention. Improve medical facilities — prenatal and postnatal care, and medically-assisted deliveries — to reduce maternal and infant mortality. Education acts on knowledge; this acts on infrastructure. Different pillar, so it counts separately.

Strategy three, different again. Create awareness of sexually transmitted diseases and of population issues, and support research into better contraceptives. Three strategies, three genuinely different mechanisms — education, infrastructure, and awareness plus research.

<whisper>And hold one in reserve. If the question asks for four, or for more, add the statutory ban on prenatal sex-determination. It is on the N C E R T list and it is distinct from all three above, because it is legal rather than educational or medical. Never repeat yourself when there is a fresh strategy available.
Ten seconds. This question has no depth to explore and no reasoning to reward. It is a pure recall trap, and it exists to punish guessing. Either you know the pair or you do not.
But there is one thing to notice even here, and it is the difference between the students who get it and the students who know the answer and still lose the mark.

Look at the four options. Now read the stem again. For females and males, respectively. That word respectively is doing real work — it tells you which number goes first. The order of the question decides the order of the answer.
The figures. Eighteen years for females. Twenty one years for males. So the answer is b.

Now look at how the other three are constructed, because it tells you what each one is fishing for. Option a, eighteen and eighteen, removes the difference between the sexes entirely — it catches someone who remembers eighteen and nothing else. Option d, sixteen and eighteen, invents both figures and catches a pure guess.

<whisper>And option c. Twenty one and eighteen. Look at it carefully. Those are the right two numbers. It is the correct pair, in the wrong order. This option is not aimed at students who do not know — it is aimed at students who do know, and who skimmed the word respectively. That is a crueller trap than simply not knowing, and it is the one that fires most often.
So the cue. Ladies first, and the smaller number. Female eighteen, male twenty one. It fixes both the values and the order in one phrase, and the order is where the mark is actually lost.

And one cross-fact, since we are on numbers. Do not let this collide with the other years in the chapter. Family planning is nineteen fifty one. Medical termination of pregnancy legalised is nineteen seventy one. The sex-determination ban is nineteen ninety four. The marriageable ages are eighteen and twenty one. Four different sets of numbers, and the exam mixes them deliberately.
This looks like a memory question and it is not. It is a one-principle question, and if you hold the principle you do not need to remember anything about India at all.
The principle. A population grows when births outpace deaths. That is it. Now test every option against that single line, and watch three of them die immediately.
Look at the board. Three red rows and one green. Notice that each red row fails for a different reason — they are not lazy distractors.

Option a. Rising death rate and rising birth rate. Stop at the first half. A rising death rate? That is the opposite of what happened, and it is the opposite of the whole historical point — healthcare lowered the death rate. Wrong.

Option c. Declining birth rate with rising death rate. Test it against the principle. Fewer births, more deaths. That combination shrinks a population. It does not explode it. It is not a weaker explanation — it is the reverse of one.
Option d. Equal birth and death rates. Births equal deaths means zero net growth. The population is stable, by definition. If this were the answer there would be no explosion to explain.

Option b. Declining death rate, declining maternal and infant mortality rate, with a continuing high birth rate. Test it. Deaths falling, births staying high — so births outpace deaths, and by a widening margin. That is exactly the gap we drew earlier. It captures the real mechanism. The answer is b.

<whisper>And one exam-craft observation worth carrying beyond this question. Notice that b is also the longest and most detailed option. On mechanism questions, the fully-specified option is very often the right one — not because long means correct, but because a real mechanism genuinely has several parts, and the wrong options are short precisely because they are simplistic. Do not distrust an option for being detailed.

This assertion reason has an unusual shape, and spotting the shape saves you the third step entirely. Here the reason is not a true fact that fails to explain — it is simply false. And a false reason ends the question early.
Same discipline as always. Test A alone. Then test R alone. And notice — if R turns out false, you never need to ask about the link at all, because a false statement cannot explain anything.
Look at the board. The assertion box is bordered green. The reason box is bordered red. That asymmetry is the answer, and you can see it before reading a word.
Test A. Has a statutory ban been placed on the use of amniocentesis for sex-determination? Yes. That is the P C P N D T Act of nineteen ninety four, brought in to curb female foeticide. A is true.

Now test R, on its own. It claims amniocentesis cannot detect any genetic disorder of the foetus. Is that true? No — it is the opposite of true. Detecting genetic and chromosomal disorders is amniocentesis's primary, legitimate purpose. That is what the test is for. Down syndrome, haemophilia. R is false.

And now stop. A is true, R is false. That is option c, and you are done. There is no third step, because asking whether a false statement explains a true one is not a meaningful question. Notice how much time that saves — the shape of the answer resolved before you did any thinking about causation.

<curious>But look more closely at how R was built, because it is beautifully designed. R is not a random false statement. It is precisely the false statement a student would produce if they believed the wrong thing — namely, that amniocentesis itself had been outlawed.

Follow that student's reasoning. Something got banned. Bans are for bad things. So amniocentesis must be bad. So it must not do anything good — it must not detect disorders. And R now sounds plausible to them, so they accept it and mark a.

<whisper>The cure is the precision from the concept section. The ban is on the misuse — sex-determination. It is not on the legitimate diagnostic use, which is legal, valuable, and continuing. Hold those two apart and R is obviously false on sight. Conflate them and this question is designed to take you.

<curious>अब एक सच में असहज सवाल। क्या कोई medical technology एक ही वक़्त में अच्छी और बुरी हो सकती है? Amniocentesis इस chapter का जवाब है, और क़ानून इसे कैसे संभालता है — exam असल में यही test करता है।
Board देखिए। ऊपर एक green strip, बीच में एक red chain, और उस पर एक legal cross खिंचा हुआ। Green और red — दोनों एक ही technique हैं।

पहले technique. Amniocentesis foetus के चारों तरफ़ मौजूद amniotic fluid का sample निकालता है। उस fluid में foetal cells होती हैं, और वो cells chromosomal pattern और कोई भी genetic disorder बता देती हैं। Sample precisely notice कीजिए — amniotic fluid. Maternal blood नहीं, placental tissue नहीं, cervical mucus नहीं। Options तीनों offer करते हैं।

और legitimate purpose सच में क़ीमती है। यह Down syndrome या haemophilia जैसी conditions को जन्म से पहले पकड़ता है, जब family तैयारी कर सके या clinician planning कर सके। यह एक अच्छा tool है। इसे पकड़े रखिए, क्योंकि अब हम कुछ भयानक बताने वाले हैं।

अब misuse. Chromosomal pattern सिर्फ़ disorders नहीं बताता। वो foetal sex भी बता देता है। और इसीलिए इस test का दुरुपयोग prenatal sex-determination के लिए हुआ, और वहाँ से female foeticide — यानी female foetuses का चुनकर abortion — और एक ख़तरनाक तरीक़े से skewed sex ratio. Technique नहीं बदली। मक़सद बदला।

यह इतना क्यों मायने रखता है? क्योंकि जो society लगातार female foetuses का abortion करती है, उसका sex ratio male-biased और skewed हो जाता है, और नतीजे पीढ़ियों तक चलते हैं। आबादी में कम women. बिगड़े marriage patterns. जड़ जमाया gender injustice. इसलिए यह ban सिर्फ़ individual foetuses को नहीं, society के demographic और social संतुलन को बचाता है।

तो जवाब में strategy statutory है। ऐसी techniques के sex-determination वाले इस्तेमाल पर ban. India में यह है Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques Act, nineteen ninety four का, यानी P C P N D T Act. यह prenatal sex-determination को punishable offence बनाता है।

<whisper>और अब वो precision जो exam असल में test कर रहा है। सिर्फ़ misuse ban है। Diagnostic use legal है, क़ीमती है, और चलता रहता है। Amniocentesis पर पाबंदी नहीं है — sex-determination पर है। Students लगातार इन दोनों को मिला देते हैं, और एक पूरा assertion reason question इसी confusion पर बना है। और limiting condition याद रखिए — चूँकि यह practice सिर्फ़ statutes से नहीं, attitudes से चलती है, इसलिए sex education और awareness को enforcement जितना ही ज़रूरी माना जाता है।

जाने से पहले एक cross-link. Female foeticide असल में किया कैसे जाता है? Medical termination of pregnancy के दुरुपयोग से। Sex-determination foetus की पहचान करता है; M T P pregnancy ख़त्म करता है। वही अगला subtopic है, और यहीं दोनों जुड़ते हैं।
पाँच marks, और यह subtopic का सबसे predictable question है। जो दोनों तरफ़ काटता है — structure हो तो मुफ़्त marks, न हो तो बहकता हुआ आधा answer.
Command words पढ़िए। Define, और suggest three. ये दो अलग tasks हैं, दो अलग mark allocations के साथ। तो आपके answer के दो दिखने वाले हिस्से होने चाहिए, और examiner को दोनों एक नज़र में दिख जाएँ।

और देखिए suggest three माँगता क्या है। तीन distinct strategies. एक ही strategy को अलग कपड़े पहनाकर तीन बार नहीं। जो script कहे लोगों को शिक्षित कीजिए, फिर students को पढ़ाइए, फिर जानकारी फैलाइए — उसने एक strategy तीन बार लिखी है और उसे एक का ही मिलेगा।
Board देखिए। ऊपर एक definition strip, नीचे तीन अलग boxes, और एक reserve box. यही full-mark answer की shape है।

Definition, एक line में, चारों aspects. Reproductive health यानी reproduction के physical, emotional, behavioural, और social aspects में total well-being. Paragraph मत लिखिए। Social मत छोड़िए। एक line, चार शब्द।
Strategy एक. Schools में sex education लाइए, ताकि myths दूर हों। और purpose clause जोड़िए — ताकि myths दूर हों — क्योंकि यह दिखाता है कि आपको सिर्फ़ label नहीं, mechanism पता है।

Strategy दो, और notice कीजिए यह बिलकुल अलग तरह का intervention है। Medical facilities सुधारिए — prenatal और postnatal care, और medically-assisted deliveries — ताकि maternal और infant mortality घटे। Education knowledge पर act करता है; यह infrastructure पर। अलग pillar, इसलिए अलग गिना जाएगा।

Strategy तीन, फिर से अलग। Sexually transmitted diseases और population issues की awareness बनाइए, और बेहतर contraceptives की research को support कीजिए। तीन strategies, तीन सच में अलग mechanisms — education, infrastructure, और awareness plus research.

<whisper>और एक reserve में रखिए। अगर question चार माँगे, या ज़्यादा, तो prenatal sex-determination पर statutory ban जोड़िए। यह N C E R T की list पर है और ऊपर वाली तीनों से अलग है, क्योंकि यह legal है, educational या medical नहीं। जब नई strategy मौजूद हो तो ख़ुद को कभी मत दोहराइए।
दस second. इस question में न खोजने को गहराई है, न इनाम देने को reasoning. यह शुद्ध recall trap है, और यह अंदाज़े को सज़ा देने के लिए बना है। या तो जोड़ी पता है, या नहीं।
लेकिन यहाँ भी एक चीज़ notice करने लायक़ है, और यही फ़र्क़ है उन students में जो इसे सही करते हैं और उनमें जिन्हें answer पता है और फिर भी mark गँवा देते हैं।

चारों options देखिए। अब stem दोबारा पढ़िए। Females और males के लिए, respectively. वो शब्द respectively असली काम कर रहा है — यह बताता है कि पहले कौन सा number आएगा। Question का order ही answer का order तय करता है।
Figures. Females के लिए eighteen years. Males के लिए twenty one years. तो answer है b.

अब देखिए बाक़ी तीन कैसे बने हैं, क्योंकि इससे पता चलता है हर एक किसे पकड़ने आया है। Option a, eighteen और eighteen, sexes के बीच फ़र्क़ ही मिटा देता है — यह उसे पकड़ता है जिसे eighteen याद है और बस। Option d, sixteen और eighteen, दोनों figures गढ़ लेता है और शुद्ध अंदाज़े को पकड़ता है।

<whisper>और option c. Twenty one और eighteen. इसे ध्यान से देखिए। ये सही दोनों numbers हैं। सही जोड़ी, ग़लत order में। यह option उन students के लिए नहीं है जिन्हें पता नहीं — यह उनके लिए है जिन्हें पता है, और जिन्होंने respectively शब्द skim कर दिया। यह न जानने से ज़्यादा क्रूर trap है, और यही सबसे ज़्यादा चलता है।
तो cue. Ladies first, and the smaller number. Female eighteen, male twenty one. यह एक ही phrase में values भी तय करता है और order भी, और mark असल में order पर ही जाता है।

और एक cross-fact, क्योंकि हम numbers पर हैं। इसे chapter के बाक़ी सालों से टकराने मत दीजिए। Family planning — nineteen fifty one. Medical termination of pregnancy legalised — nineteen seventy one. Sex-determination ban — nineteen ninety four. Marriageable ages — eighteen और twenty one. चार अलग numbers के सेट, और exam इन्हें जान-बूझकर मिलाता है।
यह memory question लगता है और है नहीं। यह एक-principle वाला question है, और principle पकड़ में हो तो आपको India के बारे में कुछ भी याद रखने की ज़रूरत नहीं।
Principle. आबादी तब बढ़ती है जब births, deaths से आगे निकल जाएँ। बस इतना। अब हर option को इसी एक line से test कीजिए, और देखिए तीन तुरंत मर जाते हैं।
Board देखिए। तीन red rows और एक green. Notice कीजिए हर red row अलग वजह से fail होती है — ये आलसी distractors नहीं हैं।
Option a. Rising death rate और rising birth rate. पहले आधे पर ही रुक जाइए। Rising death rate? यह तो जो हुआ उसका उलटा है, और पूरे ऐतिहासिक point का भी उलटा — healthcare ने death rate घटाई थी। ग़लत।

Option c. Declining birth rate के साथ rising death rate. Principle से test कीजिए। कम births, ज़्यादा deaths. यह combination आबादी को सिकोड़ता है। फोड़ता नहीं। यह कमज़ोर explanation नहीं है — यह explanation का उलटा है।
Option d. Equal birth और death rates. Births बराबर deaths यानी zero net growth. आबादी definition से ही stable है। यह answer होता तो explain करने के लिए कोई explosion ही नहीं होता।

Option b. Declining death rate, declining maternal और infant mortality rate, और साथ में continuing high birth rate. Test कीजिए। Deaths गिर रहे, births ऊँचे बने हुए — तो births, deaths से आगे, और फ़ासला चौड़ा होता हुआ। यही तो वो gap है जो हमने पहले बनाया था। यह असली mechanism पकड़ता है। Answer है b.

<whisper>और एक exam-craft की बात जो इस question से आगे भी काम आएगी। Notice कीजिए b सबसे लंबा और सबसे detailed option भी है। Mechanism वाले questions में fully-specified option अक्सर सही होता है — इसलिए नहीं कि लंबा यानी सही, बल्कि इसलिए कि असली mechanism के सच में कई हिस्से होते हैं, और ग़लत options छोटे इसीलिए हैं क्योंकि वो simplistic हैं। किसी option पर detailed होने की वजह से शक मत कीजिए।

इस assertion reason की shape अनोखी है, और shape पहचान लेने से तीसरा step पूरा बच जाता है। यहाँ reason कोई सच्चा fact नहीं है जो explain करने में चूक जाए — यह सीधा झूठा है। और झूठा reason question को जल्दी ख़त्म कर देता है।
Discipline वही पुरानी। A अकेला test कीजिए। फिर R अकेला। और notice कीजिए — अगर R झूठा निकला, तो link पूछने की ज़रूरत ही नहीं, क्योंकि झूठा statement कुछ explain नहीं कर सकता।
Board देखिए। Assertion box का border green है। Reason box का border red. यही asymmetry answer है, और यह एक शब्द पढ़े बिना दिख जाता है।
A test कीजिए। क्या amniocentesis के sex-determination वाले इस्तेमाल पर statutory ban लगा है? हाँ। यह P C P N D T Act है, nineteen ninety four का, जो female foeticide रोकने के लिए लाया गया। A true है।

अब R test कीजिए, अकेले। यह कहता है कि amniocentesis foetus का कोई भी genetic disorder detect नहीं कर सकता। क्या यह सच है? नहीं — यह सच का उलटा है। Genetic और chromosomal disorders पकड़ना ही amniocentesis का primary, legitimate purpose है। Test है ही इसके लिए। Down syndrome, haemophilia. R झूठा है।

और अब रुक जाइए। A true, R false. यह option c है, और आपका काम ख़त्म। तीसरा step है ही नहीं, क्योंकि यह पूछना कि झूठा statement सच्चे को explain करता है या नहीं — यह कोई अर्थपूर्ण सवाल नहीं है। Notice कीजिए कितना वक़्त बचा — answer की shape तय हो गई, इससे पहले कि आप causation के बारे में कुछ सोचते।

<curious>लेकिन ग़ौर से देखिए R बनाया कैसे गया है, क्योंकि यह बेहद ख़ूबसूरती से design किया गया है। R कोई random झूठा statement नहीं है। यह ठीक वही झूठा statement है जो एक student तब गढ़ेगा जब वो ग़लत बात मान बैठे — कि amniocentesis पर ही पाबंदी लग गई है।

उस student की सोच follow कीजिए। कुछ ban हुआ। Ban बुरी चीज़ों पर लगते हैं। तो amniocentesis बुरा होगा। तो यह कुछ अच्छा नहीं करता होगा — यह disorders detect नहीं करता होगा। और अब R उसे plausible लगने लगता है, तो वो उसे मान लेता है और a mark कर देता है।

<whisper>इलाज वही precision है जो concept section में थी। Ban misuse पर है — sex-determination पर। Legitimate diagnostic use पर नहीं, जो legal है, क़ीमती है, और चालू है। इन दोनों को अलग रखिए तो R देखते ही झूठा है। मिला दीजिए तो यह question आपको ले जाने के लिए ही बना है।

board_events.text: The four pitfalls that cost marks here
PITFALL 1: Truncating the WHO definition. It is FOUR aspects — physical, emotional, behavioural and social. Dropping 'social' loses the mark.
PITFALL 2: Mixing up the years. Family planning to 1951. MTP legalised to 1971. Sex-determination ban (PCPNDT) to 1994. Keep them apart.
PITFALL 3: Thinking amniocentesis is banned outright. Only its use for SEX-DETERMINATION is banned; its diagnostic use is legal and valuable.
PITFALL 4: Swapping the marriageable ages. Female 18, male 21 — never the reverse. And read 'respectively'.
PRO-TIP for speed

When a question gives you OUTCOMES — falling MMR and IMR, smaller families, better STD cure — and asks what they show, the answer is almost always 'improved reproductive health / a successful RCH strategy'.
Read indicators, then conclusion, in ONE step. Do not narrate each trend separately.
Memory hook for the years: '51 plans the family, 71 ends the pregnancy' — 1951 family planning, 1971 MTP. And 94 polices the scan.
MTP = induced abortion

board_events.text: MTP, also called INDUCED ABORTION, is the intentional or voluntary termination of a pregnancy before full term — before the foetus becomes viable on its own.
The word that matters is INDUCED. This is a deliberate medical procedure.
That is exactly what separates it from a SPONTANEOUS ABORTION — a natural miscarriage that the body undergoes on its own. Unintended, and not a procedure at all.
'Before full term' carries a precise idea: the pregnancy is terminated before the foetus becomes VIABLE — before it could survive independently outside the womb.
Viability is NOT a fixed instant. With modern neonatal care it is generally placed around the start of the THIRD trimester.
This is one reason both medicine and law concentrate safe, straightforward termination in the EARLIER weeks of pregnancy.
MTP as a public-health measure

board_events.text: Unwanted pregnancies HAPPEN — through casual unprotected sex, through failure of a contraceptive, or through sexual assault.
And sometimes continuing a pregnancy would seriously endanger the mother, or the foetus, or both.
Before legal, safe abortion existed, women turned to UNSAFE, clandestine procedures — which caused high maternal mortality and morbidity.
Legalising MTP was, at heart, a PUBLIC-HEALTH MEASURE: to make a necessary procedure safe.
Regulation converts a dangerous back-alley practice into a safe medical one.
So the 'strict conditions' are NOT bureaucratic hurdles. They exist to keep the procedure safe, and to block its misuse.
The single most important biological idea in the topic

board_events.text: Imagine a train that is safest to disembark from while it is still moving slowly near the platform. The longer you wait, the faster and more dangerous it becomes to step off. Early pregnancy is the 'slow' phase.

IN THE FIRST TRIMESTER (up to about 12 weeks): the embryo or foetus is small and NOT YET intimately connected to the maternal blood supply and uterine wall. The placental attachment is still developing.
So termination at this stage involves LESS TISSUE, LESS BLEEDING RISK, and a SIMPLER PROCEDURE. It is comparatively safe.
IN THE SECOND TRIMESTER: the foetus becomes INTIMATELY ASSOCIATED with maternal tissue — a mature, vascular placental connection.
So termination now means disrupting a far more integrated structure: more bleeding, more risk, greater medical complexity.
This is the single most important biological idea in the topic. Every safety question, and one assertion-reason, runs on it.
And it is why BOTH the medical advice (do it early) and the legal limits (tighter conditions later) push toward early termination.
The distinction the exam asks directly

board_events.text: CONTRACEPTION prevents fertilisation or implantation. It acts BEFORE a pregnancy exists.
MTP ends a pregnancy that is already ESTABLISHED. It acts AFTER a pregnancy exists.
MTP is NOT a method of contraception. This is the most-tested conceptual point in the subtopic.
Treating abortion as routine birth control is both medically wrong and NOT the law's intent.
MTP is also NOT intended as a tool of POPULATION CONTROL — its role in reducing population is insignificant.
It exists for the HEALTH AND WELFARE OF THE INDIVIDUAL. That is the whole purpose.

segments.text: Four pitfalls close this subtopic. Three of them are about numbers or words rather than biology, which is exactly why students who understand the topic still lose marks on it.

Pitfall one. Truncating the World Health Organisation definition. It is four aspects — physical, emotional, behavioural, and social. Students remember physical, feel confident, and stop early. Social is the one that gets dropped, and dropping it loses the mark. Four, every time.

Pitfall two, and this is the biggest scorer for examiners in the whole subtopic. Mixing up the years. Family planning is nineteen fifty one. Medical termination of pregnancy was legalised in nineteen seventy one. The sex-determination ban, the P C P N D T Act, is nineteen ninety four. Three years, three completely different things, and the exam offers them as each other's distractors constantly.

Pitfall three. Thinking amniocentesis is banned outright. It is not. Only its use for sex-determination is banned. Its diagnostic use — detecting Down syndrome, haemophilia — is legal, valuable, and ongoing. An entire assertion reason question is built on this confusion, and we have just done it.

Pitfall four. Swapping the marriageable ages. Female eighteen, male twenty one. Never the reverse. And read the word respectively in the stem, because the trap option offers the right numbers in the wrong order.
Now the pro-tip, and it is the highest-yield reading habit in this subtopic.

<whisper>When a question gives you outcomes — falling maternal and infant mortality rate, more assisted deliveries, smaller families, better cure of sexually transmitted diseases — and asks what they show, do not start explaining each trend. The answer is almost always one line. Improved reproductive health, or a successful R C H strategy.

Read indicators, then conclusion, in one step. The question looks analytical and it is actually a recognition task. The moment you see a cluster of indicators, you already know the intended answer — so write it first and only then justify it if the marks demand.

And a hook for the years, since they cost more marks than anything else here. Fifty one plans the family, seventy one ends the pregnancy. Nineteen fifty one, family planning. Nineteen seventy one, medical termination of pregnancy. And add the third yourself — ninety four polices the scan. Three years, one rhythm, and the cross-fact trap stops working.
The last subtopic. And it is the one where a single word does almost all the definitional work — miss that word and every answer you write here will be half right at best.
Look at the board. Two boxes, side by side, and they describe things that sound similar and are not the same event at all.

The definition first. Medical termination of pregnancy, also called induced abortion, is the intentional or voluntary termination of a pregnancy before full term — before the foetus becomes viable on its own. Say that as one sentence, because that is how a two-mark question wants it.
<curious>Now the word that matters. Induced. Everything hangs on it. Induced means this is a deliberate medical procedure — somebody decided, and somebody performed it.

And that is exactly what separates it from a spontaneous abortion, which is a natural miscarriage that the body undergoes on its own. Notice the contrast is not about outcome — both end a pregnancy. It is about intention. One is chosen and carried out; the other simply happens. A two-mark distinguish question lives entirely on that difference.

Now unpack the other phrase, before full term. It is not vague. It carries a precise idea. The pregnancy is terminated before the foetus becomes viable — before it could survive independently outside the womb. Viability is the real boundary, and full term is just how we say it.

But here is a subtlety worth holding. Viability is not a fixed instant. There is no single moment at which a foetus switches from non-viable to viable. It shifts with medical capability, and with modern neonatal care it is generally placed around the start of the third trimester.

And that fuzziness is precisely why both medicine and law concentrate safe, straightforward termination in the earlier weeks of pregnancy. Earlier is further from the boundary, and further from the boundary is simpler on every axis. Hold that thought — it is the shape of this whole subtopic.

Before the biology and before the law, a prior question. Why does a society need a legal route for this at all? Because the answer is the reason the act exists, and a two-mark question asks it directly.
Look at the board. Three boxes across the top, and they converge on one line at the bottom. Follow the arrow and you have the whole argument.

Start with the honest premise. Unwanted pregnancies happen. Through casual unprotected sex. Through the failure of a contraceptive — and remember, no reversible method is fully effective, so failure is not hypothetical. And through sexual assault. Those are the three routes, and none of them can be legislated out of existence.

Second premise. Sometimes continuing a pregnancy would seriously endanger the mother, or the foetus, or both. Here the pregnancy may be entirely wanted, and still be dangerous. That is a different situation from the first, and the law treats it differently.

<curious>Now the crucial part, and it is historical rather than biological. What actually happened before legal, safe abortion existed? Did the procedure stop happening? It did not. Women turned to unsafe, clandestine procedures — performed by unqualified people, in unhygienic conditions. And those caused high maternal mortality and morbidity. The demand did not disappear. Only the safety did.

So here is the sentence to write. Legalising medical termination of pregnancy was, at heart, a public-health measure — to make a necessary procedure safe. It was not a statement about morality. It was a response to women dying.

Say it another way, because this framing answers several questions at once. Regulation converts a dangerous back-alley practice into a safe medical one. The law did not create the procedure. It brought an existing procedure indoors, where it could be done properly.

<whisper>And that gives you the answer to the question students find hardest here. Why must strict conditions be followed? Because the strict conditions are not bureaucratic hurdles. They are the entire point. They exist to keep the procedure safe, and to block its misuse. Remove the conditions and you have recreated the back alley with a licence.

If you learn one thing from this subtopic, learn this. It is the biology under every safety question, it is the reason the law is shaped the way it is, and it is the answer to an assertion reason that NEET likes.

Look at the two panels. Same organ, same pregnancy, two moments in time. On the left the connection is dotted and forming. On the right it is thick, branching, and vascular. That difference is the entire topic.

Start with the picture. Imagine a train that is safest to disembark from while it is still moving slowly near the platform. The longer you wait, the faster it goes and the more dangerous it becomes to step off. Early pregnancy is the slow phase. Nothing in that analogy is about morality — it is purely about physics, and here, about anatomy.

Now the first trimester, up to about twelve weeks. The embryo or foetus is small, and — this is the operative clause — it is not yet intimately connected to the maternal blood supply and the uterine wall. The placental attachment is still developing. It is a work in progress, not a finished structure.

And the consequences follow directly from that anatomy. Termination at this stage involves less tissue. Less bleeding risk. A simpler procedure. That is why it is comparatively safe. Notice you did not have to memorise safe — you derived it from how attached the foetus is.

Now the second trimester. The foetus becomes intimately associated with maternal tissue. The placental connection is now mature and vascular — a dense, blood-rich junction between two bodies. Those exact words, intimately associated, are the ones the exam wants.

<whisper>So termination now means disrupting a far more integrated structure. More bleeding. More risk. Greater medical complexity. The procedure did not get harder because a rule changed. It got harder because the anatomy changed.
That is the single most important biological idea in the topic. Every safety question runs on it, and so does one assertion reason we will do shortly. If you can say why, the whole subtopic opens.

And notice what it explains beyond safety. It is why both the medical advice and the legal limits point the same way. Medicine says do it early because the tissue is less attached. The law says tighter conditions later because the risk is higher. Two different systems, one underlying anatomy, the same conclusion — earlier is better.
One line, and it decides more marks in this subtopic than anything else. Medical termination of pregnancy is not a contraceptive. Not a poor one, not a last-resort one. Not one at all.

Look at the board. Two boxes, and read the bottom strip of each — acts before a pregnancy exists, acts after a pregnancy exists. That is the whole distinction, and it is about timing, not about severity.

Contraception prevents fertilisation, or prevents implantation. Go back through subtopic one and check — every single family did exactly that. Natural avoided the meeting. Barrier blocked it. Hormonal stopped ovulation. The intra uterine device made the uterus hostile. Surgical cut the transport. All of them act before a pregnancy exists.

Medical termination of pregnancy does something categorically different. It ends a pregnancy that is already established. Fertilisation happened. Implantation happened. There is a pregnancy, and the procedure ends it. It acts after.

<whisper>So say it flatly. M T P is not a method of contraception. This is the most-tested conceptual point in the subtopic — it appears as a direct question, as an option in a which-statement-is-correct, and inside assertion reason stems. If an option calls M T P a routine method of contraception, or says M T P prevents fertilisation, it is wrong on sight.

And the reasoning is not merely definitional. Treating abortion as routine birth control is both medically wrong and not the law's intent. Medically wrong, because a procedure carrying real risk cannot sensibly replace a pill that carries almost none. Not the law's intent, because the act was written for need, not for convenience.

There is a second thing M T P is not, and students miss this one more often. It is not intended as a tool of population control. You might think a procedure performed forty five to fifty million times a year must move the population numbers. It does not meaningfully — its role in reducing population is insignificant.

So what is it for? It exists for the health and welfare of the individual. One woman, one situation, one medical decision. That is the whole purpose, and if a question asks about M T P and population in the same breath, that is the answer it wants.
चार pitfalls इस subtopic को बंद करते हैं। इनमें से तीन biology के बारे में नहीं, numbers या शब्दों के बारे में हैं — और इसीलिए topic समझने वाले students भी यहाँ marks गँवाते हैं।

Pitfall एक. World Health Organisation की definition को काट देना। यह चार aspects है — physical, emotional, behavioural, और social. Students physical याद कर लेते हैं, confident हो जाते हैं, और जल्दी रुक जाते हैं। Social ही छूटता है, और छूटते ही mark जाता है। चार, हर बार।

Pitfall दो, और यही पूरे subtopic में examiners का सबसे बड़ा scorer है। सालों को मिला देना। Family planning — nineteen fifty one. Medical termination of pregnancy nineteen seventy one में legalise हुआ। Sex-determination ban, यानी P C P N D T Act, nineteen ninety four का है। तीन साल, तीन बिलकुल अलग चीज़ें, और exam इन्हें लगातार एक-दूसरे का distractor बनाकर पेश करता है।

Pitfall तीन. यह मान लेना कि amniocentesis पूरी तरह ban है। नहीं है। सिर्फ़ इसका sex-determination वाला इस्तेमाल ban है। इसका diagnostic use — Down syndrome, haemophilia पकड़ना — legal है, क़ीमती है, और चालू है। एक पूरा assertion reason question इसी confusion पर बना है, और हम अभी-अभी वो कर चुके हैं।
Pitfall चार. Marriageable ages उलट देना। Female eighteen, male twenty one. उलटा कभी नहीं। और stem में respectively शब्द पढ़िए, क्योंकि trap option सही numbers ग़लत order में देता है।
अब pro-tip, और यह इस subtopic की सबसे ज़्यादा फ़ायदे वाली reading habit है।

<whisper>जब question आपको outcomes दे — गिरती maternal और infant mortality rate, ज़्यादा assisted deliveries, छोटे families, sexually transmitted diseases की बेहतर cure — और पूछे कि ये क्या दिखाते हैं, तो हर trend explain करना शुरू मत कीजिए। Answer लगभग हमेशा एक line है। बेहतर reproductive health, या एक successful R C H strategy.

Indicators पढ़िए, फिर conclusion, एक ही step में। Question analytical दिखता है और असल में recognition task है। जिस पल indicators का cluster दिखे, आपको मनचाहा answer पहले से पता है — तो पहले वही लिखिए, और marks माँगें तभी justify कीजिए।

और सालों के लिए एक hook, क्योंकि यहाँ किसी और चीज़ से ज़्यादा marks इन्हीं पर जाते हैं। इक्यावन family plan करता है, इकहत्तर pregnancy ख़त्म करता है। Nineteen fifty one, family planning. Nineteen seventy one, medical termination of pregnancy. और तीसरा ख़ुद जोड़िए — चौरानवे scan पर पहरा देता है। तीन साल, एक लय, और cross-fact trap काम करना बंद कर देता है।
आख़िरी subtopic. और यही वो है जहाँ एक अकेला शब्द लगभग पूरा definitional काम करता है — वो शब्द छूटा तो यहाँ आपका हर answer ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा आधा सही होगा।
Board देखिए। दो boxes, आमने-सामने, और ये ऐसी चीज़ें बताते हैं जो सुनने में एक जैसी लगती हैं और एक ही घटना बिलकुल नहीं हैं।

पहले definition. Medical termination of pregnancy, जिसे induced abortion भी कहते हैं, यानी pregnancy का intentional या voluntary termination, full term से पहले — इससे पहले कि foetus अपने दम पर viable हो जाए। इसे एक ही sentence की तरह बोलिए, क्योंकि two-mark question इसे ऐसे ही चाहता है।
<curious>अब वो शब्द जो मायने रखता है। Induced. सब कुछ इसी पर टिका है। Induced यानी यह एक deliberate medical procedure है — किसी ने तय किया, और किसी ने इसे perform किया।

और ठीक यही इसे spontaneous abortion से अलग करता है, जो एक natural miscarriage है जिससे body अपने आप गुज़रती है। Notice कीजिए contrast outcome का नहीं है — दोनों pregnancy ख़त्म करते हैं। यह intention का है। एक चुना और किया जाता है; दूसरा बस हो जाता है। पूरा two-mark distinguish question इसी फ़र्क़ पर ज़िंदा है।

अब दूसरा phrase खोलिए — before full term. यह अस्पष्ट नहीं है। इसमें एक precise idea है। Pregnancy तब terminate होती है जब foetus viable न हुआ हो — यानी वो womb के बाहर स्वतंत्र रूप से जी न सके। असली सीमा viability है, और full term तो बस कहने का तरीक़ा है।

लेकिन एक बारीक़ी पकड़ने लायक़ है। Viability कोई तय पल नहीं है। ऐसा कोई एक moment नहीं जब foetus non-viable से viable में बदल जाए। यह medical capability के साथ खिसकती है, और आधुनिक neonatal care के साथ इसे आम तौर पर third trimester की शुरुआत के आसपास रखा जाता है।

और यही धुँधलापन ठीक वो वजह है कि medicine और law, दोनों safe और सीधा termination pregnancy के शुरुआती हफ़्तों में केंद्रित करते हैं। पहले यानी सीमा से दूर, और सीमा से दूर यानी हर axis पर आसान। इसे पकड़े रखिए — यही पूरे subtopic की shape है।
Biology से पहले और law से पहले, एक पहला सवाल। समाज को इसके लिए legal route चाहिए ही क्यों? क्योंकि इसी का जवाब वो वजह है जिससे यह act मौजूद है, और two-mark question इसे सीधा पूछता है।
Board देखिए। ऊपर तीन boxes, और वो नीचे एक line पर आकर मिलते हैं। Arrow follow कीजिए और पूरी दलील आपके पास है।

ईमानदार premise से शुरू कीजिए। Unwanted pregnancies होती हैं। Casual unprotected sex से। किसी contraceptive के fail होने से — और याद रखिए, कोई भी reversible method पूरी तरह effective नहीं है, तो failure काल्पनिक नहीं है। और sexual assault से। ये तीन रास्ते हैं, और इनमें से किसी को क़ानून बनाकर मिटाया नहीं जा सकता।

दूसरा premise. कभी-कभी pregnancy जारी रखना mother को, या foetus को, या दोनों को गंभीर ख़तरे में डाल देता। यहाँ pregnancy पूरी तरह wanted हो सकती है, और फिर भी ख़तरनाक। यह पहली situation से अलग है, और law इसे अलग तरह से देखता है।

<curious>अब सबसे अहम हिस्सा, और यह biological नहीं, ऐतिहासिक है। Legal, safe abortion के मौजूद होने से पहले असल में हुआ क्या? क्या procedure होना बंद हो गया? नहीं हुआ। Women unsafe, clandestine procedures की तरफ़ गईं — जो अयोग्य लोगों ने, गंदी हालत में किए। और उनसे high maternal mortality और morbidity हुई। माँग ग़ायब नहीं हुई। सिर्फ़ safety ग़ायब हुई।

तो लिखने वाली sentence यह है। Medical termination of pregnancy को legal करना, अपने मूल में, एक public-health measure था — एक ज़रूरी procedure को safe बनाने के लिए। यह morality पर बयान नहीं था। यह women के मरने का जवाब था।

इसे दूसरे तरीक़े से कहिए, क्योंकि यह framing एक साथ कई questions का जवाब देती है। Regulation एक ख़तरनाक back-alley practice को safe medical practice में बदल देता है। Law ने procedure बनाया नहीं। उसने एक मौजूद procedure को अंदर लाया, जहाँ वो ठीक से हो सके।

<whisper>और इससे आपको उस सवाल का जवाब मिलता है जो students को यहाँ सबसे मुश्किल लगता है। Strict conditions क्यों माननी चाहिए? क्योंकि strict conditions bureaucratic अड़चनें नहीं हैं। वही तो पूरी बात हैं। वो procedure को safe रखने के लिए हैं, और उसके misuse को रोकने के लिए। Conditions हटा दीजिए तो आपने licence के साथ वही back alley दोबारा बना दी।
इस subtopic से अगर एक चीज़ सीखनी है, तो यह सीखिए। यही हर safety question के नीचे की biology है, यही वजह है कि law इस shape में है, और यही उस assertion reason का जवाब है जो N E E T को पसंद है।
दोनों panels देखिए। वही organ, वही pregnancy, समय के दो पल। बाईं तरफ़ connection dotted है और बन रहा है। दाईं तरफ़ वो मोटा है, शाखाओं वाला, और vascular. यही फ़र्क़ पूरा topic है।

तस्वीर से शुरू कीजिए। एक train सोचिए जिससे उतरना तभी सबसे safe है जब वो platform के पास धीरे चल रही हो। जितना रुकेंगे, वो उतनी तेज़ होगी और उतरना उतना ख़तरनाक। Early pregnancy वही slow phase है। इस analogy में morality कुछ नहीं है — यह पूरी तरह physics की बात है, और यहाँ anatomy की।

अब first trimester, लगभग twelve weeks तक। Embryo या foetus छोटा है, और — यही operative clause है — वो अभी maternal blood supply और uterine wall से intimately connected नहीं है। Placental attachment अभी बन ही रहा है। यह चालू काम है, तैयार ढाँचा नहीं।

और नतीजे सीधे उसी anatomy से निकलते हैं। इस stage पर termination में कम tissue शामिल होता है। कम bleeding risk. आसान procedure. इसीलिए यह comparatively safe है। Notice कीजिए आपको safe रटना नहीं पड़ा — आपने इसे इससे निकाला कि foetus कितना जुड़ा हुआ है।

अब second trimester. Foetus maternal tissue से intimately associated हो जाता है। Placental connection अब mature और vascular है — दो शरीरों के बीच एक घना, ख़ून से भरा जोड़। यही exact शब्द, intimately associated, exam को चाहिए।

<whisper>तो अब termination का मतलब है कहीं ज़्यादा integrated ढाँचे को तोड़ना। ज़्यादा bleeding. ज़्यादा risk. ज़्यादा medical जटिलता। Procedure इसलिए मुश्किल नहीं हुआ कि कोई rule बदल गया। वो इसलिए मुश्किल हुआ कि anatomy बदल गई।
यही इस topic का सबसे अहम biological idea है। हर safety question इसी पर चलता है, और वो assertion reason भी जो हम थोड़ी देर में करेंगे। अगर आप why बता सकते हैं, तो पूरा subtopic खुल जाता है।

और देखिए यह safety से आगे क्या समझाता है। यही वजह है कि medical advice और legal limits, दोनों एक ही तरफ़ इशारा करते हैं। Medicine कहती है जल्दी कीजिए क्योंकि tissue कम जुड़ा है। Law कहती है बाद में सख़्त conditions क्योंकि risk ज़्यादा है। दो अलग systems, एक ही underlying anatomy, वही नतीजा — पहले बेहतर है।

एक line, और यह इस subtopic में बाक़ी किसी भी चीज़ से ज़्यादा marks तय करती है। Medical termination of pregnancy contraceptive नहीं है। कोई घटिया contraceptive नहीं, कोई last-resort contraceptive नहीं। बिलकुल भी नहीं।
Board देखिए। दो boxes, और हर एक की नीचे वाली strip पढ़िए — pregnancy होने से पहले act करता है, pregnancy होने के बाद act करता है। यही पूरा distinction है, और यह timing की बात है, गंभीरता की नहीं।

Contraception fertilisation रोकता है, या implantation रोकता है। Subtopic एक में वापस जाकर देखिए — हर एक family ने ठीक यही किया। Natural ने meeting टाली। Barrier ने रोकी। Hormonal ने ovulation बंद किया। Intra uterine device ने uterus को hostile बनाया। Surgical ने transport काटा। ये सब pregnancy होने से पहले act करते हैं।

Medical termination of pregnancy बिलकुल अलग श्रेणी का काम करता है। यह उस pregnancy को ख़त्म करता है जो पहले से established है। Fertilisation हो चुका। Implantation हो चुका। Pregnancy मौजूद है, और procedure उसे ख़त्म करता है। यह बाद में act करता है।

<whisper>तो सीधा कहिए। M T P contraception का method नहीं है। यह subtopic का सबसे ज़्यादा पूछा जाने वाला conceptual point है — यह सीधे question की तरह आता है, which-statement-is-correct के option की तरह आता है, और assertion reason के stems के अंदर भी। अगर कोई option M T P को routine method of contraception कहे, या कहे कि M T P fertilisation रोकता है, वो देखते ही ग़लत है।

और वजह सिर्फ़ definitional नहीं है। Abortion को routine birth control मानना medically भी ग़लत है और law का इरादा भी नहीं। Medically ग़लत, क्योंकि जो procedure असली risk रखता है वो उस pill की जगह समझदारी से नहीं ले सकता जिसमें लगभग कोई risk नहीं। Law का इरादा नहीं, क्योंकि act ज़रूरत के लिए लिखा गया था, सुविधा के लिए नहीं।

एक दूसरी चीज़ भी है जो M T P नहीं है, और students इसे और ज़्यादा भूलते हैं। यह population control का tool नहीं है। आपको लग सकता है कि जो procedure साल में forty five से fifty million बार होता है, वो तो आबादी के आँकड़े हिला ही देगा। असल में नहीं — आबादी घटाने में इसकी भूमिका insignificant है।

तो यह है किसलिए? यह व्यक्ति की health और welfare के लिए है। एक woman, एक situation, एक medical फ़ैसला। यही पूरा purpose है, और अगर कोई question M T P और population को एक ही साँस में पूछे, तो जवाब यही चाहिए।

board_events.text: SCALE (NCERT-illustrative): nearly 45 to 50 MILLION MTPs are performed worldwide each year.
That is about ONE-FIFTH of all conceived pregnancies in a year. A sanity-check figure worth remembering.
METHODS depend on the gestational stage: PHARMACOLOGICAL (medical), using drugs in the earliest weeks; or SURGICAL, for later or more advanced cases.
WHEN MTP IS ADVISED, reason 1: an UNWANTED PREGNANCY — from casual unprotected intercourse, contraceptive failure, or rape.
Reason 2: when CONTINUATION would be HARMFUL or even FATAL to the mother, the foetus, or both.
Reason 3: a DIAGNOSED SERIOUS FOETAL ABNORMALITY.
MTP is meant for GENUINE NEED, not convenience — and must be done by QUALIFIED MEDICAL PERSONNEL in an APPROVED FACILITY.
MTP Act, 1971 · MTP (Amendment) Act, 2021

board_events.text: Abortion was legalised in India by the MTP ACT, 1971.
It was amended by the MTP (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021 — in force from 24 September 2021 — which raised the upper gestational limit from 20 to 24 WEEKS for special categories of women.
UP TO 20 WEEKS: the opinion of ONE registered medical practitioner (RMP).
20 TO 24 WEEKS: the opinion of TWO RMPs, for SPECIAL CATEGORIES — survivors of rape or incest, minors, differently-abled and other vulnerable women.
BEYOND 24 WEEKS: permitted ONLY for substantial foetal abnormality, on the approval of a state-level MEDICAL BOARD.
The Amendment also allows UNMARRIED WOMEN to seek MTP (e.g. on the ground of contraceptive failure), and adds a CONFIDENTIALITY clause.

The original 1971 Act capped termination at 20 weeks and, on the contraceptive-failure ground, covered only MARRIED women. The 2021 reforms were driven by repeated court petitions from rape survivors, and from women whose foetal abnormalities were detected only in the second trimester.
KEEP TWO LAYERS SEPARATE: the MEDICAL-SAFETY fact is 12 weeks (first trimester). The LEGAL framework is the 20/24-week structure. They are different questions.
On what grounds is abortion permitted under the Act?

board_events.text: THERAPEUTIC grounds: risk to the mother's LIFE, or to her physical or MENTAL health.
EUGENIC grounds: a substantial risk of serious FOETAL ABNORMALITY.
HUMANITARIAN grounds: a pregnancy resulting from RAPE or SEXUAL ASSAULT.
SOCIAL grounds: for example, the FAILURE of a contraceptive method.
Each ground answers a DIFFERENT question: whose risk? whose abnormality? how did the pregnancy begin? what are the circumstances?
Note what is NOT a ground: the SEX of the foetus. That is the punishable misuse — never a legal ground.

board_events.text: SIGNIFICANCE: MTP safely removes unwanted or harmful pregnancies, and protects the HEALTH AND LIFE of the mother.
But note: MTP is NOT intended as a tool of population control or contraception. Its role in reducing population is insignificant — it exists for the health and welfare of the INDIVIDUAL.
DRAWBACKS: it is misused for FEMALE FOETICIDE after illegal sex-determination. It raises emotional, ethical, religious and social questions. And it is UNSAFE if done late, or by unqualified persons.
THE MISUSE CHAIN: a foetus is sexed — often via the misuse of amniocentesis — and a healthy FEMALE foetus is then aborted.
Repeated across a population, this skews the SEX RATIO in favour of males: fewer women, disrupted marriage patterns, and entrenched gender injustice over a generation.
TWO legal countermeasures: the ban on sex-determination (PCPNDT Act, 1994 — subtopic 03), and the strict regulation of MTP itself (who may perform it, when, and on what grounds).
MTP performed for a genuine medical or humanitarian reason is LEGITIMATE. It is the SEX-SELECTIVE MISUSE that is the evil. Keep the two apart.
Q. State any two situations in which MTP is advised, and explain why strict conditions must be followed during MTP procedures. [CBSE, 2-3 marks]
Two separate tasks in one question. 'State any two' is a list; 'explain why' is a reason. Both are marked, so write both visibly.
