board_events.text: TWO SITUATIONS (any two): (i) the pregnancy is unwanted, due to contraceptive failure or rape; (ii) continuation is dangerous to the mother and/or the foetus; (iii) a diagnosed serious foetal abnormality.
WHY STRICT CONDITIONS, reason 1: to ensure the procedure is performed SAFELY, by qualified medical personnel in approved facilities — because unsafe or late abortions cause maternal mortality.
WHY STRICT CONDITIONS, reason 2: to PREVENT MISUSE for sex-selective (female) foeticide.
Give BOTH reasons. Most scripts give safety and stop — the misuse reason is a separate mark.
And the framing that earns the explanation mark: strict conditions are not bureaucratic hurdles. They are what CONVERTS a dangerous practice into a safe medical one.

segments.text: Three things in this section, and all three are directly askable. A figure, a method split, and a list of three reasons. None of it is hard. All of it is precise.
Look at the board. Scale and methods across the top, then three green boxes underneath. Those three boxes are a two-mark answer waiting to be written.

The scale first. Nearly forty five to fifty million medical terminations of pregnancy are performed worldwide each year. That is the N C E R T illustrative figure, and C U E T asks for the order of magnitude directly.

<whisper>And the second half of the figure is the one that makes it stick. That is about one-fifth of all conceived pregnancies in a year. One in five. It is also a sanity check — if an option offers forty five to fifty billion, you can reject it instantly, because that exceeds the number of pregnancies the world has. The unit is the trap, not the number.

Now the methods, and it is a simple split governed by one variable. The method depends on how advanced the pregnancy is. Pharmacological abortion, also called medical abortion, uses drugs to end a pregnancy in the earliest weeks. Surgical abortion is used for later or more advanced cases. Same principle as everything else here — the stage decides.

Now the three reasons M T P is advised, and I want you to notice they are genuinely different in kind. Reason one, an unwanted pregnancy. And that has three sources of its own — casual unprotected intercourse, contraceptive failure, or rape. Here the pregnancy itself is the problem.

Reason two is completely different. When continuation would be harmful, or even fatal, to the mother, the foetus, or both. The pregnancy may be entirely wanted. It is the danger that triggers the procedure, not the wanting.

Reason three, a diagnosed serious foetal abnormality. Note the word diagnosed — this is not a suspicion or a preference. Something has been detected, by a test, and that connects straight back to the prenatal diagnostics we met in the last subtopic.

<whisper>And now the clause that governs all three. M T P is meant for genuine need, not convenience. And it must be done by qualified medical personnel in an approved facility. Those two conditions are not decoration — remember what happened when they were absent. Every one of those three reasons is a need. None of them is a preference.
Now the law. And I want to warn you before we start — this section contains the single most common mix-up in the whole chapter, and it is not between two laws. It is between the law and the biology.
Look at the timeline. Colour bands across the top, then three boxes for the three legal windows. And notice the red strip at the very bottom. That strip is the warning.
The founding fact. Abortion was legalised in India by the M T P Act of nineteen seventy one. That is the year C U E T asks for, and it is the year that gets confused with nineteen fifty one.

Then the modernisation. It was amended by the M T P Amendment Act of twenty twenty one, in force from the twenty fourth of September, twenty twenty one. Its headline change — it raised the upper gestational limit from twenty weeks to twenty four weeks, for special categories of women.

Now the three-tier structure, and learn it as a ladder where each rung adds an authority. Up to twenty weeks, you need the opinion of one registered medical practitioner. One doctor. That is the ordinary case.

From twenty to twenty four weeks, you need the opinion of two registered medical practitioners, and only for special categories. Who are those? Survivors of rape or incest, minors, differently-abled women, and other vulnerable women. Two doctors, and a restricted category — the bar rises on both axes at once.

Beyond twenty four weeks, the ladder changes character. It is permitted only for substantial foetal abnormality, and only on the approval of a state-level Medical Board. Not two doctors — a board. And only one ground survives.

Two more reforms in twenty twenty one, and they are easy marks. The Amendment allows unmarried women to seek M T P, for instance on the ground of contraceptive failure. And it adds a confidentiality clause, protecting the woman's identity.

<curious>And why did those changes come? Because of what the original nineteen seventy one Act did. It capped termination at twenty weeks, and on the contraceptive-failure ground it covered only married women. The reforms were driven by repeated court petitions — from rape survivors, and from women whose foetal abnormalities were only detected in the second trimester, by which time the old limit had already closed. The law moved because reality kept arriving after the deadline.

<whisper>Now the warning. Keep two layers separate. The medical-safety fact is twelve weeks — the first trimester, relatively safe, because the foetus is not yet intimately associated with maternal tissue. The legal framework is the twenty and twenty four week structure. These are different questions with different answers. If a stem asks when M T P is relatively safe and you answer twenty weeks, you have quoted a statute at a biology question and lost the mark.

Four grounds, four names, and the names themselves are not obvious. So do not memorise them as a flat list — notice that each one answers a different question, and the question is what fixes the name in your memory.
Look at the four boxes. Read the small grey line under each: protect the mother, about the foetus, how it began, circumstances. Four different questions.

Ground one, therapeutic. Therapy means treatment, so this ground is about the mother's health. The precise wording is risk to the mother's life, or to her physical or mental health. And do not drop that last phrase — mental health is explicitly included, and students routinely leave it out.

Ground two, eugenic. This one is about the foetus rather than the mother. A substantial risk of serious foetal abnormality. Note the qualifiers — substantial risk, serious abnormality. Not any risk, not any abnormality. The Act sets a bar.

Ground three, humanitarian, and this one asks a different question entirely — how did the pregnancy begin? A pregnancy resulting from rape or sexual assault. Nothing here is about the health of anyone. It is about the circumstances of conception.

Ground four, social. For example, the failure of a contraceptive method. And notice how this connects the chapter — subtopic one told you no reversible method is fully effective. This is the law making room for that fact.

<whisper>So run the four questions rather than the four words. Whose risk is it — the mother's? Therapeutic. Whose abnormality — the foetus's? Eugenic. How did it begin — assault? Humanitarian. What are the circumstances — a method failed? Social. Ask the question and the name arrives.

And now the most important line in this section, which is about what is missing. Look at the four grounds and notice what is not among them. The sex of the foetus is not a ground. It has never been a ground. It is the punishable misuse — and that is where this subtopic turns dark, which is exactly where we go next.

Every technique in this chapter has had a clean story. This one does not. M T P saves lives and it is also used to destroy them selectively — and the exam expects you to hold both halves at once without blurring them.
Look at the board. Green on the left, red on the right, and then the chain running along the bottom. Both sides are true simultaneously.

The significance first. M T P safely removes unwanted or harmful pregnancies, and it protects the health and life of the mother. That is a real good. Remember what preceded it — clandestine procedures and high maternal mortality. Against that baseline, this is a life-saving intervention.

But do not overclaim on its behalf, because a question is built here. M T P is not intended as a tool of population control or of contraception. Its role in reducing population is insignificant. It exists for the health and welfare of the individual. One woman, one situation.

Now the drawbacks, and there are three. It is misused for female foeticide after illegal sex-determination. It raises emotional, ethical, religious and social questions — the chapter says so openly. And it is unsafe if done late, or by unqualified persons. Notice that the third drawback is not about the procedure — it is about the procedure done wrongly.

The misuse chain, step by step. A foetus is sexed — often through the misuse of amniocentesis, which you met in the previous subtopic. And then a healthy female foetus is aborted. Healthy. There is no medical reason at any point in that chain. Sex-determination identifies; M T P executes. Two misused tools, one outcome.

And repeated across a population, this skews the sex ratio in favour of males. The consequences are not individual — they are demographic. Fewer women. Disrupted marriage patterns. Entrenched gender injustice, over a generation. One decision repeated a million times becomes a structural fact about a society.

So the law answers with two countermeasures, not one. First, the ban on sex-determination — the P C P N D T Act of nineteen ninety four, which you did in the last subtopic. Second, the strict regulation of M T P itself: who may perform it, when, and on what grounds. Block the identification, and regulate the execution. Two locks on one door.

<whisper>And here is the precision to carry out. M T P performed for a genuine medical or humanitarian reason is legitimate. It is the sex-selective misuse that is the evil. Do not let the misuse contaminate your description of the procedure — that is exactly the error the amniocentesis assertion reason punished, and the same trap is set here.
Two or three marks, and the question quietly contains two entirely separate tasks. Miss that structure and you will answer one of them beautifully and score half.

Read it again. State any two situations in which M T P is advised. And explain why strict conditions must be followed. The first is a list. The second is a reason. Both carry marks, so both must be visible on your page.
Look at the board. Situations on the left, reasons on the right. Two columns, because it is two questions.

The situations first, and you need any two of three. One, the pregnancy is unwanted, due to contraceptive failure or rape. Two, continuation is dangerous to the mother and or the foetus. Three, a diagnosed serious foetal abnormality. Pick two, state them cleanly, and move on — do not spend your time here, because the marks are waiting in the second half.

Now why strict conditions, and here is where scripts go thin. Reason one, the obvious one. To ensure the procedure is performed safely, by qualified medical personnel, in approved facilities. And add the because — unsafe or late abortions cause maternal mortality. That clause is what turns a statement into an explanation.

<whisper>Reason two, and this is the one that separates the top scripts. To prevent misuse for sex-selective female foeticide. The conditions are not only about safety. They are also a gate against a specific social evil. A student who only knows the safety answer has half the picture.

So give both reasons. Most scripts give safety and stop, because safety is the intuitive answer and it feels complete. It is not. The misuse reason is a separate mark, and it costs you one line to claim it.

And if you want the explanation mark cleanly, use the framing from the concept section. Strict conditions are not bureaucratic hurdles. They are what converts a dangerous back-alley practice into a safe medical one. That sentence shows the examiner you understand why the Act exists, not merely what it says.
इस section में तीन चीज़ें हैं, और तीनों सीधे पूछी जा सकती हैं। एक figure, एक method का बँटवारा, और तीन reasons की list. कुछ भी मुश्किल नहीं है। सब कुछ precise है।
Board देखिए। ऊपर scale और methods, फिर नीचे तीन green boxes. वो तीन boxes एक two-mark answer हैं जो लिखे जाने का इंतज़ार कर रहा है।
पहले scale. दुनिया भर में हर साल लगभग forty five से fifty million medical terminations of pregnancy होते हैं। यह N C E R T की illustrative figure है, और C U E T इसका order of magnitude सीधा पूछता है।

<whisper>और figure का दूसरा आधा वही है जो इसे चिपका देता है। यह साल की सारी conceived pregnancies का लगभग one-fifth है। पाँच में एक। यह sanity check भी है — अगर कोई option forty five से fifty billion दे, तो उसे तुरंत reject कर दीजिए, क्योंकि यह दुनिया की कुल pregnancies से ज़्यादा है। Trap unit है, number नहीं।

अब methods, और यह एक ही variable से चलने वाला सीधा बँटवारा है। Method इस बात पर depend करता है कि pregnancy कितनी आगे बढ़ी है। Pharmacological abortion, जिसे medical abortion भी कहते हैं, शुरुआती हफ़्तों में drugs से pregnancy ख़त्म करता है। Surgical abortion बाद के या ज़्यादा आगे बढ़े cases के लिए। वही principle जो यहाँ हर जगह है — stage तय करती है।

अब वो तीन reasons जिन पर M T P advise होता है, और मैं चाहता हूँ आप notice करें कि ये सच में अलग-अलग क़िस्म के हैं। Reason एक, unwanted pregnancy. और इसके अपने तीन स्रोत हैं — casual unprotected intercourse, contraceptive failure, या rape. यहाँ pregnancy ख़ुद problem है।
Reason दो बिलकुल अलग है। जब जारी रखना mother को, foetus को, या दोनों को harmful, या fatal तक हो जाए। Pregnancy पूरी तरह wanted हो सकती है। Procedure को trigger ख़तरा करता है, चाहत नहीं।

Reason तीन, diagnosed serious foetal abnormality. Diagnosed शब्द notice कीजिए — यह कोई शक या पसंद नहीं है। कुछ पकड़ा गया है, किसी test से, और यह सीधे उन prenatal diagnostics से जुड़ता है जो हम पिछले subtopic में देख चुके हैं।

<whisper>और अब वो clause जो तीनों पर लागू है। M T P genuine need के लिए है, सुविधा के लिए नहीं। और यह qualified medical personnel द्वारा, approved facility में होना चाहिए। ये दोनों conditions सजावट नहीं हैं — याद कीजिए इनके न होने पर क्या हुआ था। उन तीनों reasons में हर एक एक need है। कोई भी preference नहीं है।
अब law. और शुरू करने से पहले चेतावनी — इस section में पूरे chapter की सबसे आम गड़बड़ है, और वो दो क़ानूनों के बीच नहीं है। वो law और biology के बीच है।
Timeline देखिए। ऊपर colour bands, फिर तीन legal windows के लिए तीन boxes. और सबसे नीचे red strip notice कीजिए। वही strip चेतावनी है।
बुनियादी fact. India में abortion को M T P Act, nineteen seventy one ने legal किया। यही वो साल है जो C U E T पूछता है, और यही वो साल है जो nineteen fifty one से confuse होता है।

फिर आधुनिकीकरण। इसे M T P Amendment Act, twenty twenty one ने amend किया, जो twenty fourth September, twenty twenty one से लागू है। इसका मुख्य बदलाव — इसने upper gestational limit को twenty weeks से बढ़ाकर twenty four weeks किया, women की special categories के लिए।
अब तीन-स्तरीय ढाँचा, और इसे एक सीढ़ी की तरह सीखिए जहाँ हर पायदान एक authority जोड़ता है। Twenty weeks तक, एक registered medical practitioner की opinion चाहिए। एक doctor. यही सामान्य case है।

Twenty से twenty four weeks तक, दो registered medical practitioners की opinion चाहिए, और सिर्फ़ special categories के लिए। वो कौन हैं? Rape या incest की survivors, minors, differently-abled women, और दूसरी vulnerable women. दो doctors, और सीमित category — दोनों axes पर एक साथ bar ऊपर उठता है।

Twenty four weeks के बाद सीढ़ी का चरित्र ही बदल जाता है। यह सिर्फ़ substantial foetal abnormality के लिए allowed है, और सिर्फ़ state-level Medical Board की मंज़ूरी से। दो doctors नहीं — एक board. और सिर्फ़ एक ground बचता है।

Twenty twenty one में दो और सुधार, और ये आसान marks हैं। Amendment unmarried women को M T P माँगने की इजाज़त देता है, मसलन contraceptive failure के ground पर। और यह एक confidentiality clause जोड़ता है, जो woman की पहचान बचाता है।

<curious>और ये बदलाव आए क्यों? इसलिए कि मूल nineteen seventy one Act ने क्या किया था। उसने termination को twenty weeks पर रोका, और contraceptive-failure वाले ground पर सिर्फ़ married women को cover किया। सुधार बार-बार आई court petitions से आए — rape survivors से, और उन women से जिनके foetal abnormalities सिर्फ़ second trimester में पकड़ में आए, जब तक पुरानी limit बंद हो चुकी थी। Law इसलिए हिला क्योंकि हक़ीक़त बार-बार deadline के बाद आती रही।

<whisper>अब चेतावनी। दो layers अलग रखिए। Medical-safety वाला fact है twelve weeks — first trimester, relatively safe, क्योंकि foetus अभी maternal tissue से intimately associated नहीं है। Legal framework है twenty और twenty four week वाला ढाँचा। ये अलग सवाल हैं और इनके जवाब अलग हैं। अगर stem पूछे कि M T P कब relatively safe है और आप twenty weeks कहें, तो आपने biology के सवाल पर statute quote कर दिया और mark गँवा दिया।
चार grounds, चार नाम, और नाम ख़ुद obvious नहीं हैं। तो इन्हें flat list की तरह मत रटिए — notice कीजिए कि हर एक अलग सवाल का जवाब देता है, और वही सवाल नाम को याद में जमा देता है।
चारों boxes देखिए। हर एक के नीचे छोटी grey line पढ़िए: mother को बचाइए, foetus के बारे में, शुरू कैसे हुआ, परिस्थितियाँ। चार अलग सवाल।

Ground एक, therapeutic. Therapy यानी इलाज, तो यह ground mother की health के बारे में है। Precise wording है — mother की life को ख़तरा, या उसकी physical या mental health को। और वो आख़िरी हिस्सा मत छोड़िए — mental health साफ़-साफ़ शामिल है, और students इसे अक्सर छोड़ देते हैं।

Ground दो, eugenic. यह mother के बजाय foetus के बारे में है। Serious foetal abnormality का substantial risk. Qualifiers notice कीजिए — substantial risk, serious abnormality. कोई भी risk नहीं, कोई भी abnormality नहीं। Act एक bar तय करता है।

Ground तीन, humanitarian, और यह बिलकुल अलग सवाल पूछता है — pregnancy शुरू कैसे हुई? Rape या sexual assault से हुई pregnancy. यहाँ किसी की health की बात नहीं है। यह conception की परिस्थितियों की बात है।

Ground चार, social. मसलन, किसी contraceptive method का fail होना। और देखिए यह chapter को कैसे जोड़ता है — subtopic एक ने बताया था कि कोई reversible method पूरी तरह effective नहीं है। यह law उसी सच्चाई के लिए जगह बना रहा है।

<whisper>तो चार शब्दों की जगह चार सवाल चलाइए। Risk किसका है — mother का? Therapeutic. Abnormality किसकी — foetus की? Eugenic. शुरू कैसे हुआ — assault से? Humanitarian. परिस्थिति क्या है — method fail हुआ? Social. सवाल पूछिए, नाम अपने आप आ जाएगा।

और अब इस section की सबसे अहम line, जो इस बारे में है कि क्या ग़ायब है। चारों grounds देखिए और notice कीजिए कि इनमें क्या नहीं है। Foetus का sex ground नहीं है। यह कभी ground था ही नहीं। यह punishable misuse है — और यहीं से यह subtopic अँधेरे में मुड़ता है, और ठीक वहीं हम आगे जा रहे हैं।

इस chapter की हर technique की कहानी साफ़ रही है। इसकी नहीं है। M T P जानें बचाता है और चुन-चुनकर जानें ख़त्म करने में भी इस्तेमाल होता है — और exam चाहता है कि आप दोनों आधे एक साथ थामें, बिना उन्हें मिलाए।
Board देखिए। बाईं तरफ़ green, दाईं तरफ़ red, और नीचे चलती हुई chain. दोनों तरफ़ एक साथ सच हैं।

पहले significance. M T P unwanted या harmful pregnancies को safely हटाता है, और mother की health तथा life बचाता है। यह असली भलाई है। याद कीजिए इससे पहले क्या था — clandestine procedures और high maternal mortality. उस baseline के सामने यह जान बचाने वाला intervention है।

लेकिन इसकी तरफ़ से ज़्यादा दावा मत कीजिए, क्योंकि यहीं एक question बना है। M T P population control या contraception का tool नहीं है। आबादी घटाने में इसकी भूमिका insignificant है। यह व्यक्ति की health और welfare के लिए है। एक woman, एक situation.

अब drawbacks, और ये तीन हैं। illegal sex-determination के बाद इसका female foeticide के लिए misuse होता है। यह emotional, ethical, religious और social सवाल खड़े करता है — chapter यह खुलकर कहता है। और अगर देर से हो, या अयोग्य लोगों से हो, तो यह unsafe है। Notice कीजिए तीसरा drawback procedure के बारे में नहीं है — वो ग़लत तरीक़े से किए गए procedure के बारे में है।

Misuse chain, क़दम दर क़दम। किसी foetus का sex पता किया जाता है — अक्सर amniocentesis के misuse से, जो आप पिछले subtopic में देख चुके हैं। और फिर एक healthy female foetus का abortion कर दिया जाता है। Healthy. उस पूरी chain में कहीं कोई medical वजह नहीं है। Sex-determination पहचानता है; M T P अंजाम देता है। दो misused tools, एक नतीजा।

और आबादी भर में दोहराए जाने पर यह sex ratio को males की तरफ़ झुका देता है। नतीजे individual नहीं हैं — वो demographic हैं। कम women. बिगड़े marriage patterns. जड़ जमाया gender injustice, एक पीढ़ी में। एक फ़ैसला दस लाख बार दोहराया जाए तो वो society के बारे में structural सच बन जाता है।

तो law एक नहीं, दो countermeasures से जवाब देता है। पहला, sex-determination पर ban — P C P N D T Act, nineteen ninety four, जो आपने पिछले subtopic में किया। दूसरा, ख़ुद M T P की सख़्त regulation: कौन कर सकता है, कब, और किन grounds पर। पहचान रोकिए, और अंजाम को regulate कीजिए। एक दरवाज़े पर दो ताले।

<whisper>और अब वो precision जो साथ ले जानी है। Genuine medical या humanitarian वजह से किया गया M T P legitimate है। बुराई sex-selective misuse है। Misuse को अपने procedure के विवरण को दूषित मत करने दीजिए — यही तो वो ग़लती थी जिसे amniocentesis वाले assertion reason ने सज़ा दी थी, और वही जाल यहाँ भी बिछा है।
दो या तीन marks, और question चुपचाप दो बिलकुल अलग tasks समेटे हुए है। यह structure छूटा तो आप एक को शानदार जवाब देंगे और आधे marks पाएँगे।

दोबारा पढ़िए। M T P किन दो situations में advise होता है, बताइए। और explain कीजिए कि strict conditions क्यों माननी चाहिए। पहला एक list है। दूसरा एक reason है। दोनों पर marks हैं, तो दोनों आपके page पर दिखने चाहिए।
Board देखिए। बाईं तरफ़ situations, दाईं तरफ़ reasons. दो columns, क्योंकि ये दो questions हैं।

पहले situations, और आपको तीन में से कोई दो चाहिए। एक, pregnancy unwanted है — contraceptive failure या rape की वजह से। दो, जारी रखना mother और या foetus के लिए ख़तरनाक है। तीन, diagnosed serious foetal abnormality. दो चुनिए, साफ़-साफ़ लिखिए, और आगे बढ़िए — यहाँ वक़्त मत लगाइए, क्योंकि marks दूसरे आधे में इंतज़ार कर रहे हैं।

अब strict conditions क्यों, और यहीं scripts पतली पड़ जाती हैं। Reason एक, ज़ाहिर वाला। ताकि procedure safely हो, qualified medical personnel से, approved facilities में। और because जोड़िए — unsafe या late abortions maternal mortality करते हैं। वही clause statement को explanation में बदलता है।

<whisper>Reason दो, और यही top scripts को अलग करता है। Sex-selective female foeticide के लिए misuse रोकने के लिए। Conditions सिर्फ़ safety के बारे में नहीं हैं। वो एक ख़ास social evil के ख़िलाफ़ दरवाज़ा भी हैं। जिस student को सिर्फ़ safety वाला जवाब पता है, उसके पास आधी तस्वीर है।
तो दोनों reasons दीजिए। ज़्यादातर scripts safety देकर रुक जाती हैं, क्योंकि safety intuitive जवाब है और पूरा लगता है। है नहीं। Misuse वाला reason अलग mark है, और उसे लेने में एक line लगती है।

और अगर explanation वाला mark साफ़-साफ़ चाहिए, तो concept section वाली framing use कीजिए। Strict conditions bureaucratic अड़चनें नहीं हैं। वो वही चीज़ हैं जो एक ख़तरनाक back-alley practice को safe medical practice में बदलती हैं। यह sentence examiner को दिखाती है कि आप समझते हैं Act मौजूद क्यों है, सिर्फ़ यह नहीं कि वो कहता क्या है।

board_events.text: Q. MTP is considered relatively safe when carried out during the: (a) first trimester (b) second trimester (c) third trimester (d) full term [CUET / NEET speed-trap]
Decide the AXIS before you answer. The words 'relatively safe' make this a MEDICAL question, not a legal one.

board_events.text: ANSWER: (a). The first trimester — up to about 12 weeks — is the relatively safe window.
THE REASON, and always quote it: early on, the foetus is NOT YET intimately associated with maternal tissue.
Do NOT answer '20 weeks'. That is a LEGAL limit figure, not the medical-safety statement. This is the classic mix-up.
(b) the second trimester is the RISKIER one — it is the wrong half of the same fact. (c) and (d) are later still; full term is a delivery, not a termination.
Cue: 'earlier = safer'.

Q. Which statement about MTP is correct? (a) MTP is a routine method of contraception (b) MTP prevents fertilisation (c) MTP is the intentional termination of an established pregnancy and is not a contraceptive (d) MTP can be safely performed by anyone at any stage [NEET]
Eliminate on the contraception/safety logic. Two options confuse MTP with contraception; one confuses it with a risk-free procedure.

board_events.text: (a) and (b) both wrongly EQUATE MTP with contraception. MTP ends a pregnancy; it does not prevent one.
(d) is false: MTP needs qualified personnel and is stage-restricted. 'Anyone at any stage' contradicts both the safety biology and the Act.
(c) states BOTH truths — it terminates an established pregnancy, AND it is not a contraceptive. ANSWER: (c).
Note that (c) carries two claims joined by 'and'. Both must be true for it to win — so check both, not just the first.
Notice the whole question is just the most-tested point in costume. Know that MTP is not a contraceptive, and three of four options fall immediately.
A: MTP is comparatively unsafe during the second trimester. R: By the second trimester the foetus has become intimately associated with the maternal tissues. [NEET, high difficulty]
Same discipline: test A alone, then R alone, then ask about the link.

board_events.text: TEST A: yes — second-trimester MTP is riskier than first-trimester MTP. A is TRUE.
TEST R: yes — by the second trimester the foetus has become intimately associated with maternal tissues, through a mature vascular placenta. R is TRUE.
Is R the reason for A? YES — the deep foetal-maternal tissue connection is EXACTLY what makes late termination hazardous. ANSWER: (a).
TRAP: some pick (b), not realising the tissue association is the DIRECT CAUSE of the increased risk, rather than an unrelated true fact sitting beside it.
Compare with the amniocentesis assertion-reason in subtopic 03: there R was FALSE and the question ended at step two. Here both are true and the link is real, so you go all the way to step three.
Same format, opposite shapes — which is why you test in the SAME ORDER every time. You cannot tell by looking which shape you have been handed.
The four pitfalls that cost marks here
PITFALL 1: Calling MTP a contraceptive. It ENDS a pregnancy; contraceptives PREVENT one. This distinction is examined directly.
PITFALL 2: Confusing the MEDICAL-SAFETY figure (12 weeks) with the LEGAL limit (20/24 weeks). Both exist. Quote the right one for the question.
PITFALL 3: Forgetting the year split. MTP legalised 1971. Family planning 1951. Sex-determination ban (PCPNDT) 1994.
PITFALL 4: Ignoring the misuse angle. MTP's dark side is sex-selective female foeticide — a frequent assertion-reason theme.
PRO-TIP: decide the AXIS before you choose
If the stem stresses BIOLOGICAL SAFETY, answer 'first trimester / about 12 weeks' and cite the foetus-maternal-tissue reason.
If the stem stresses WHO or WHEN it is legal, switch to the 1971-Act and 20-24-week framework — one RMP, two RMPs, Medical Board.
Decide which axis the question is testing BEFORE choosing an option. Almost every wrong answer in this subtopic is a right answer on the wrong axis.

board_events.text: 01 CONTRACEPTION: five families — Natural, Barrier, IUD, Hormonal, Surgical ('Nice Boys Insert Hormones Surgically'). IUD mechanisms: non-medicated to phagocytosis; copper to Cu ions; hormonal to mucus + endometrium. Vasectomy = vas deferens; tubectomy = fallopian tube — both block TRANSPORT, not production. Only the condom also limits STIs.

02 STDs & INFERTILITY: NOT curable — hepatitis-B, genital herpes, HIV/AIDS. STD-but-not-RTI — AIDS + hepatitis-B. Trichomoniasis is the only protozoan. Oligo = few, azoo = none. ART: 8 or fewer to the tube (ZIFT); more than 8 to the uterus (IUT); GIFT = donor ovum to tube, in vivo; ICSI = one sperm into the ovum.

03 HEALTH & POPULATION: WHO — total well-being, physical + emotional + behavioural + SOCIAL. Family planning 1951, now RCH; India among the first. Explosion = death rate/MMR/IMR fall + birth rate stays high. Marriageable age 18 female / 21 male. Amniocentesis misused to female foeticide, banned by PCPNDT Act, 1994.

04 MTP: induced abortion = intentional termination before full term; spontaneous abortion = natural miscarriage. NOT a contraceptive. Safe in the first trimester (~12 weeks) because the foetus is not yet intimately associated with maternal tissue. ~45-50 million per year, about one-fifth of conceptions. Legal: 1971 Act; 2021 Amendment — 20 weeks (one RMP) / 20-24 (two RMPs, special categories) / beyond 24 only via Medical Board.

NUMBERS TO LOCK: fertile window days 10-17 · lactational amenorrhea ~6 months · pills 21 + 7 · emergency contraception within 72 hours · sterilisation failure under 1% · vulnerable age 15-24 · blastomere rule 8 · marriageable age 18/21 · MTP safe ~12 weeks · legal 20/24 weeks.
YEARS: 1951 family planning · 1971 MTP Act · 1994 PCPNDT Act · 2021 MTP Amendment. Hook: '51 plans the family, 71 ends the pregnancy, 94 polices the scan.'

THE FOUR CROSS-CHAPTER DISTINCTIONS the exam lives on: transport vs production (sterilisation) · STD vs RTI (location, not route) · gametes vs embryos (the uterus destroys one, accepts the other) · medical safety vs legal limit (12 weeks vs 20/24 weeks).
Every one of those four is the same skill: two things that are both true, kept apart. That is what this chapter has really been teaching.

segments.text: This looks like a one-second question, and for most students it is. But it sits on top of the single most common confusion in the subtopic, so let us do it properly rather than quickly.

Before you look at a single option, decide the axis. Read the stem — relatively safe. Those two words tell you this is a medical question, about biology. It is not a legal question, about the Act. Decide that first and the answer follows.
Look at the board. The answer on the left in green, and over on the right, the figure that is not the answer.
The answer is a, the first trimester. Up to about twelve weeks. That is the relatively safe window, and it is the N C E R T statement.

But do not just carry the answer — carry the reason, because in a written paper the figure alone is not the full mark. Early on, the foetus is not yet intimately associated with maternal tissue. Less attachment, less tissue, less bleeding, simpler procedure. Quote that and you have shown the biology rather than the memory.

<whisper>And now the trap this whole subtopic has been warning you about. Do not answer twenty weeks. Twenty weeks is a legal limit figure — it is when you need one registered medical practitioner rather than two. It is not the medical-safety statement. If the option list offers twelve weeks and twenty weeks together, the safety question wants twelve. Every time.

Quickly, the other three. Option b, the second trimester, is the riskier one — it is the wrong half of exactly the same fact, which is what makes it tempting. Options c and d are later still, and full term is not a termination at all — that is a delivery.

So carry the cue out of here. Earlier equals safer. And carry the discipline too — read the stem, decide the axis, and only then answer. Biological safety means first trimester and twelve weeks. Legal limits mean the Act and the twenty to twenty four week structure. Two axes, two answers, and the stem always tells you which one it wants.
This question has no hidden depth, and that is worth saying plainly. It is the most-tested point in the subtopic, wearing a costume. If you hold one idea, three options fall on sight.
The idea, once more. Contraception prevents a pregnancy. M T P ends one that already exists. Now run down the options with that single blade.
Look at the board. Three red rows, one green, and notice that two of the red rows fail for the same reason.

Options a and b together, because they make the same mistake. Option a says M T P is a routine method of contraception. Option b says M T P prevents fertilisation. Both wrongly equate M T P with contraception. M T P ends a pregnancy; it does not prevent one. Fertilisation has already happened by the time M T P is on the table. Both eliminated, on one idea.

Option d. M T P can be safely performed by anyone at any stage. Two falsehoods packed into one short sentence. Anyone is wrong — it needs qualified medical personnel in an approved facility. At any stage is wrong — it is stage-restricted, by the biology and by the Act. This option contradicts both halves of the subtopic at once.

<whisper>Option c. M T P is the intentional termination of an established pregnancy, and is not a contraceptive. That states both truths, and they are the two truths this entire subtopic has been building. The answer is c.

One point of exam craft before we leave, and it generalises well beyond this question. Notice that option c carries two claims joined by the word and. It terminates an established pregnancy, and it is not a contraceptive. For a compound option to win, both halves must be true — so check both. A common trick is to pair a true first half with a false second half, and students who stop reading at the comma walk straight into it.

And step back to see the shape. This whole question is just the most-tested point in disguise. Know that M T P is not a contraceptive, and know that it ends an established pregnancy, and you did not solve this question — you recognised it.
The last worked question of the chapter, and it is a gift — provided you have understood section forty three rather than memorised it. Everything here follows from that one piece of anatomy.
Same discipline, one final time. Test the assertion alone. Test the reason alone. Only then ask about the link. Never form an overall impression first.
Look at the board. Both boxes bordered the same colour, and then an arrow between them. That arrow is the third judgement, and it is the one that decides between a and b.
Test A. Is M T P comparatively unsafe during the second trimester? Yes. Second-trimester termination is riskier than first-trimester termination. That is the N C E R T statement. A is true.

Test R, on its own and forgetting A. By the second trimester, has the foetus become intimately associated with the maternal tissues? Yes — a mature, vascular placental connection has formed. That is a true statement about pregnancy, independent of any question about safety. R is true.

Now the third question, and ask it precisely. Is R the reason for A? Do not ask whether both sound related. Ask whether the tissue association is what causes the risk. And it is — exactly and directly. Disrupting a deeply integrated, blood-rich structure is what produces more bleeding, more risk, more complexity. R is not merely consistent with A. R is the mechanism of A. Both true, R explains A. The answer is a.

<whisper>So why do students pick b? Because b is for when both are true but unrelated, and the two statements here sound like they come from different registers — one about safety, one about anatomy. A student who never asked why late termination is risky has no link to see, so the two facts sit side by side looking like neighbours. But they are not neighbours. One is the cause of the other.

And now close the loop with the chapter. Compare this with the amniocentesis assertion reason from subtopic three. There, R was false, and the question ended at step two — you never reached the link. Here, both are true and the link is real, so you go all the way to step three. Same format, opposite shapes.

That is precisely why you test in the same order every time. You cannot tell from looking which shape you have been handed. A alone, R alone, then the link. The order protects you from both kinds of question, and you never need to know in advance which one is in front of you.
Four pitfalls to close the subtopic. And notice something about them — none is about difficult biology. Every one is about mixing up two things that are both true.

Pitfall one. Calling M T P a contraceptive. It ends a pregnancy; contraceptives prevent one. This distinction is examined directly, in almost every format the papers use. If you take one line out of this subtopic, take that one.

Pitfall two, and this is the specific one this subtopic exists to guard against. Confusing the medical-safety figure with the legal limit. Twelve weeks is the safety fact — the first trimester, relatively safe. Twenty and twenty four weeks are legal limits. Both figures are real and both are correct answers, to different questions. Quote the right one.

Pitfall three. Forgetting the year split. M T P was legalised in nineteen seventy one. Family planning began in nineteen fifty one. The sex-determination ban, the P C P N D T Act, is nineteen ninety four. Three years, and the papers offer them as each other's distractors constantly.

Pitfall four. Ignoring the misuse angle. M T P's dark side is sex-selective female foeticide, and it is a frequent assertion reason theme. A student who has learnt only the clean public-health story will not see it coming.
Now the pro-tip, and it is the single most useful habit in this subtopic. Decide the axis before you choose.

<whisper>If the stem stresses biological safety — words like safe, safest, relatively safe, risk — answer first trimester, about twelve weeks. And cite the reason: the foetus is not yet intimately associated with maternal tissue. That is the biology axis.

If the stem stresses who may do it, or when it is permitted, or under what conditions — switch axes entirely. Now you are on the law. The nineteen seventy one Act, the twenty to twenty four week framework, one registered medical practitioner up to twenty weeks, two for twenty to twenty four in special categories, and a Medical Board beyond that.

So decide which axis the question is testing before choosing an option. And here is why it matters more than it looks. Almost every wrong answer in this subtopic is a right answer on the wrong axis. Twenty weeks is not nonsense — it is a real, correct figure, standing in the wrong place. The exam is not testing whether you know the facts. It is testing whether you know which fact was asked for.
One board, four subtopics, and the whole chapter. This is not new material — it is the revision map you come back to the night before. Let us walk it once so you know what is on it.
Look at the board. Four quadrants, one per subtopic, colour-coded the way we studied them. If you can reconstruct each quadrant from its heading alone, you are ready.

Quadrant one, contraception. Five families — Natural, Barrier, I U D, Hormonal, Surgical. Nice Boys Insert Hormones Surgically. The three I U D mechanisms kept apart: non-medicated to phagocytosis, copper to copper ions, hormonal to mucus plus endometrium. Vasectomy is the vas deferens, tubectomy is the fallopian tube, and both block transport, not production. And only the condom also limits sexually transmitted infections.

Quadrant two, sexually transmitted diseases and infertility. The not-curable trio: hepatitis B, genital herpes, H I V or AIDS. The S T D but not R T I pair: AIDS and hepatitis B. Trichomoniasis is the only protozoan. Oligo means few, azoo means none. And the transfer rule as one phrase — eight or fewer to the tube by ZIFT, more than eight to the uterus by IUT. GIFT is a donor ovum to the tube, in vivo. ICSI is one sperm into the ovum.

Quadrant three, health and population. The World Health Organisation definition — total well-being, physical, emotional, behavioural, and social, all four. Family planning in nineteen fifty one, now R C H, and India among the first countries. The explosion: death rate and maternal and infant mortality fall while the birth rate stays high. Marriageable age eighteen female, twenty one male. And amniocentesis misused to female foeticide, banned by the P C P N D T Act of nineteen ninety four.

Quadrant four, medical termination of pregnancy. Induced abortion is intentional termination before full term; spontaneous abortion is a natural miscarriage. It is not a contraceptive. It is safe in the first trimester, about twelve weeks, because the foetus is not yet intimately associated with maternal tissue. Forty five to fifty million a year, about one-fifth of conceptions. And the legal ladder — the nineteen seventy one Act, the twenty twenty one Amendment, one registered medical practitioner up to twenty weeks, two for twenty to twenty four in special categories, and beyond twenty four only through a Medical Board.

Now the numbers, all in one place, because scattered numbers are what fail under pressure. Fertile window, days ten to seventeen. Lactational amenorrhea, about six months. Pills, twenty one plus seven. Emergency contraception within seventy two hours. Sterilisation failure under one percent. Vulnerable age, fifteen to twenty four. The blastomere rule, eight. Marriageable age, eighteen and twenty one. M T P safe at about twelve weeks, legal at twenty and twenty four.

And the years, which cost more marks than anything else in this chapter. Nineteen fifty one, family planning. Nineteen seventy one, the M T P Act. Nineteen ninety four, the P C P N D T Act. Twenty twenty one, the M T P Amendment. Fifty one plans the family, seventy one ends the pregnancy, ninety four polices the scan.

<whisper>And now the four distinctions the exam actually lives on. Transport versus production, in sterilisation. S T D versus R T I — a question of location, not of route. Gametes versus embryos — the uterus destroys one and accepts the other. And medical safety versus legal limit — twelve weeks against twenty and twenty four.

Look at those four together and notice they are the same skill wearing four costumes. In every one, two things are both true, and the whole task is keeping them apart. Sperm are still made and cannot travel. AIDS is sexually transmitted and is not a tract infection. The uterus is right for an embryo and wrong for a gamete. Twelve weeks is correct and so is twenty. That is what this chapter has really been teaching you — not more facts, but the discipline of holding two true things in their proper places.
यह एक-second का question लगता है, और ज़्यादातर students के लिए है भी। लेकिन यह इस subtopic की सबसे आम confusion के ऊपर बैठा है, तो इसे जल्दी नहीं, ठीक से करते हैं।

एक भी option देखने से पहले axis तय कीजिए। Stem पढ़िए — relatively safe. ये दो शब्द बताते हैं कि यह medical question है, biology के बारे में। यह legal question नहीं है, Act के बारे में। पहले यह तय कीजिए, answer अपने आप आएगा।
Board देखिए। बाईं तरफ़ green में answer, और दाईं तरफ़ वो figure जो answer नहीं है।
Answer है a, first trimester. लगभग twelve weeks तक। यही relatively safe window है, और यही N C E R T का statement है।
